title: t18842: fix(pulse-merge): route CI/review repair for worker PRs that use For/Ref (GH#36260)
body:
## Summary

Worker PRs that name their work issue with `For #N` or `Ref #N` instead of a closing keyword were never routed to CI or review repair. The pulse logged "routing to CI fix-worker" and then returned without a diagnostic, on every cycle. PR #36213 (`For #36212`) has had a failing required `Framework Validation` since 09:14Z with no repair attempt. Partial deliveries and checkpoints use `For`/`Ref` on purpose, so this left those PRs open indefinitely.

## Root cause

- `_pmp_stage_required_checks` (`pulse-merge.sh`) passes the target from `_extract_linked_issue`, which reads closing keywords only. For `For #N` PRs that target is empty.
- `_check_pr_merge_gates` does resolve the explicit `For`/`Ref` identity for `origin:worker` PRs, but only into a gate-local variable. That keeps partial work out of post-merge issue closing.
- `_route_pr_resolve_work_issue` (`pulse-merge-process.sh`) resolves `For`/`Ref` only when `kind=conflict` (GH#33763). For `ci` and `review` it calls `_recover_interactive_pr_work_issue`, which returns 1 for any PR not labelled `origin:interactive`. The `|| return 1` then skips `_route_pr_has_linked_issue`, the only step that logs.

Production evidence from the maintainer `pulse.log` at 09:53Z: "worker-briefed auto-merge: PR #36213 … issue #36212, link=non-closing reference", then the CI-drift rebase, then "routing to CI fix-worker". No `_dispatch_ci_fix_worker:` line follows.

## Change

- Non-conflict kinds with no closing target now resolve the work issue with `_extract_pr_work_issue … explicit`. That is the standalone `For`/`Ref` identity the merge gate already trusts, with no title inference. The resolved issue is used only as the repair target, never to close anything.
- When interactive recovery fails, the resolver now continues to the existing "has no linked issue for <kind> repair routing" log instead of returning silently.
- Conflict routing is unchanged. All downstream guards still apply: origin labels, ownership and hold labels, the closed-issue guard, the terminal-route guard, and in-place repair.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh`: clean.
- An ad-hoc harness ran the real `_route_pr_to_fix_worker` and resolvers against `origin/main` and against this branch, with GitHub reads stubbed:

| Case | `origin/main` | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| Worker PR with `For #36212`, ci (the #36213 shape) | rc=1, nothing logged | routed: `kind=ci issue=36212` |
| Worker PR with `For #36212`, review | rc=1, nothing logged | routed: `kind=review issue=36212` |
| Worker PR with no reference | rc=1, nothing logged | rc=1, logs "has no linked issue for ci repair routing" |
| Live interactive PR with `For #42` | rc=1, nothing logged | rc=1, logs "retains active origin:interactive ownership" |
| Ambiguous `For #1` + `Ref #2` | rc=1, nothing logged | rc=1, logs the ambiguity and no linked issue |
| `For` only under a "Related" heading | rc=1, nothing logged | rc=1, logs no linked issue |
| `Resolves #77`, ci | routed, issue 77 | unchanged |
| `For #55`, conflict | routed, issue 55 | unchanged |

- Existing suites all pass:
  - `test-pulse-merge-fix-worker-dispatch.sh`: 52/52
  - `test-pulse-merge-ci-repair-routing.sh`: 79/79
  - `test-pulse-merge-pr-context.sh`: 45/45

  - `test-pulse-merge-superseded-duplicates.sh`: 31/31

  - `test-pulse-merge-closing-contradiction.sh`: rc=0

- Post-deploy check: the next `For`/`Ref` worker PR with terminal CI failures should log `_dispatch_ci_fix_worker:` in `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`.

title: t18844: fix(cloudron-release): reconcile held worker bump PRs in the approval routine
body:
## Summary

Worker release handoffs for Cloudron package bumps could not request maintainer approval while PR checks were pending, so they deferred to automation. The r924 approval routine only processed approval-request issues that already existed. As a result, held bump PRs never reached the maintainer. Their findings stayed assigned and `status:in-review`, and newer findings were deferred behind them. Obsolete bumps stacked up indefinitely: `marcusquinn/aidevops-cloudron-app` had held PRs #225, #233 and #236, no open approval requests, and newest finding #239 deferred.

`release_process` now reconciles held worker PRs after it processes the approval issues (`release_reconcile_held` in `.agents/scripts/cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh`):

- The newest held worker PR that main does not already bundle gets its approval request once its checks are terminal-green. Pending checks wait for the next routine run.
- Older unsigned upstream bumps are superseded: their PRs are closed (branches kept for audit), with their findings and any unsigned approval requests, when main or the requested PR already bundles the upstream.
- Fail-closed boundaries (`#aidevops:trust-boundary`):
  - Signed, stale or unverifiable approvals are never superseded.
  - Human PRs, non-upstream PRs and PRs whose head, labels or state changed since listing are retained.
  - Only OWNER/MEMBER own-line monitor markers identify a finding.
  - API errors stop the process before any write.
- Dry runs (default without `--apply`) never write.

`describe_r924` documents the handoff, and `TODO.md` gains t18844.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-release-approval.sh` exits 0. The 8 new held-PR cases cover request/supersede, pending checks, signed approval, unsigned request, dry run, changed PR, untrusted finding marker and API errors.
- Mutation check: disabling the signed-approval guard makes `held: a signed approval is never superseded` fail with an unexpected `pr-close`.
- Review fix (7c74a23859): a trusted linked issue without a monitor marker no longer emits a misaligned finding row; the new regression case fails against the old filter and passes with the fix.
- `shellcheck -x` is clean on the helper, test and `core-routines.sh`. The pre-commit string-literal ratchet passes. `complexity-regression-helper.sh check --base origin/main --working-tree` reports no new violations.
- A read-only dry run against the real package repo reports: request approval for #236; supersede #225 (main already bundles upstream 3.39.75); supersede #233 (#236 bundles the newer v3.39.87).

## Post-merge

After deploy, the next r924 run with `--apply` should leave one pending approval request for #236 and close #225/#233 with their findings. The maintainer still signs with `sudo aidevops approve issue <N> <repo>`; this PR adds no new authority.

Resolves #36268

title: t18845: fix(cloudron-release): provision release approval labels; decouple failed request from supersession
body:
## Summary

Routine r924 (cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh process --apply) has exited 1 on every run since v3.39.104. release_request() created the approval-only issue with --label no-auto-dispatch in a managed package repo that lacks that label, and gh_create_issue intentionally never creates caller-supplied labels (GH#34003). The PR hold labels were already applied, so each run left a half-processed request. The failure also aborted release_reconcile_held() before its supersede loop, so obsolete held bumps that main already bundles were never closed. Fix: (1) managed-label-provisioning-lib.sh gains a canonical release-approval set (release-approval-required, hold-for-review, no-auto-dispatch) and managed_labels_ensure_release_approval_set, following managed_labels_ensure_approval_set (GH#34071 is the same defect class on the edit path). (2) release_request() provisions that set before its first PR label write, replacing the unconditional gh label create --force write; a converged repo costs one label read and no writes; unknown label state fails closed before any hold or issue write. (3) release_held_target() still reports its target when the request fails; release_reconcile_held() counts the failure and continues, so request-independent supersession (main already bundles upstream) proceeds and request-dependent supersession still waits for a real request.



## Files Changed

.agents/reference/dispatch-timing.md, .agents/scripts/cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh, .agents/scripts/managed-label-provisioning-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-release-approval.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-managed-label-provisioning.sh, TODO.md, todo/tasks/t18845-brief.md

title: t18846: fix(pulse-merge): skip partial parent closeout for TODO-projection PRs and closed issues
body:
## Summary

Partial parent closeout (pulse-merge-issue-closeout.sh) treated every `For #N` / `Ref #N` reference in a merged PR body as a delivered slice of a still-open parent. TODO-projection PRs (issue-sync TODO publication and pulse TODO handoff) carry `Ref #N` purely for audit linkage, so each merge posted a false "Partial Parent Closeout" comment, including on issues that were already closed. Those comments are counted as cost receipts by dispatch-dedup-cost.sh, so the noise also skews dispatch decisions.

Changes:
- `_pm_extract_partial_parent_reference` now skips PR bodies carrying `<!-- aidevops:issue-sync-todo-pr -->` or `<!-- aidevops:pulse-todo-handoff id=` in addition to the existing planning-publication marker (GH#36230). A forged marker can only suppress a comment, so marker-only matching is safe.
- `_pm_handle_partial_parent_closeout` reads `.state` from the already-fetched issue JSON and returns before posting when the issue is closed; the comment asserts the parent remains open, which is false for a closed issue.
- Focused coverage in `tests/test-pulse-merge-partial-parent-closeout.sh` for both projection markers, the closed-issue guard, and the open-issue positive path.



## Files Changed

title: GH#36321: bound upstream watch REST cost and serialize retries
body:
## Summary

Bound release summaries to one 10-item listing with metadata from that response; remove per-tag name/date requests. Serialize upstream checks using a stale-PID-recoverable directory lock, persist attempts before execution, and back off for a full hour after failure while retaining the daily success gate.

## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/auto-update-freshness-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/upstream-watch-helper-check.sh

## Decisions

Cap every release range at the newest 10 entries, with a visible truncation notice, to guarantee constant network cost even when the old tag is missing. Changes stay within the two issue-scoped files. Independent review findings on Bash 3.2 ownership and long-failure backoff were repaired and runtime-rechecked.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** High
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — ShellCheck and bash -n pass for both changed files; upstream watch mode suite passes 35 cases and issue gate suite passes 18 cases. Focused runtime checks pass concurrent skip, stale PID recovery, immediate failure retry suppression, successful daily gating, state-write failure fail-closed behavior, and missing/found/current tag summaries with exactly two API invocations per range. Repeated runtime checks with BASHPID unset verify fallback lock PID equals the executing check process. A live isolated cmd_check against marcusquinn/aidevops with an absent baseline tag performs four REST endpoint calls (latest release, latest commit, bounded listing, latest release notes) plus gh auth status; gh-api-instrument.sh logs five logical invocations, not an exact quota-cost measurement. Issue publication was disabled only in the temporary verification shell. The unrelated TypeScript typecheck cannot start because tsc dependencies are absent on this runner; pre-push explicitly defers it to CI.

## Regression Evidence

The portable part of this change is the lock-owner PID fallback when `BASHPID` is unavailable. Exercising it needs concurrent background subshells, real sleeps and a forced Bash 3.2 interpreter with the `shared-constants.sh` re-exec guard suppressed (`AIDEVOPS_BASH_REEXECED=1`). The existing upstream-watch suites have no harness for timing-dependent concurrent freshness checks, and adding one would be new test infrastructure. The maintainer interactive session instead ran an out-of-tree runtime harness against the real `check_upstream_watch` and `_show_release_diff` at head `ae72b08983` and again at `27b6b3fe4d`, under both `/bin/bash` 3.2.57 and Homebrew bash 5.3.20, with identical results:

- Two concurrent checks: the watch script ran once, the second check logged "already running — skipping", and the lock was removed afterwards.
- A failed check followed by an immediate re-tick: one run, `last_upstream_watch_attempt` recorded, the second tick was skipped by the 3600 s gate, and no success stamp was written.
- A stale lock owned by dead PID 999999 was recovered and the check ran once.
- `_show_release_diff rtk-ai/rtk no-such-tag-v0 <latest>` (rtk has more than 599 releases) made 2 `gh` calls, showing the 10 newest entries plus a truncation notice. Before this change it made 2 calls per release in the repository's history.

Resolves #36321.

- Read release summary metadata in one bounded listing instead of per-tag lookups or unbounded pagination.
- Serialize upstream freshness checks with a stale-PID-recoverable directory lock.
- Persist attempts before running and enforce a one-hour retry gate after failures.

## Scope

Only `.agents/scripts/upstream-watch-helper-check.sh` and `.agents/scripts/auto-update-freshness-lib.sh` change.

## Verification

ShellCheck and Bash syntax checks pass. Existing upstream watch mode (35 cases) and issue gate (18 cases) suites pass. Focused runtime verification is complete, including concurrent execution, portable PID ownership, failure backoff and a live isolated production check.

The push hook deferred the unrelated TypeScript typecheck to CI because runner dev dependencies (`tsc`) are not installed. No TypeScript files change.

title: GH#36349: fix(lifecycle): keep schema-1 session admission observe-only
body:
## Summary

On installs whose worker-lifecycle store is still schema 1, the OpenCode plugin and the Claude guard refused **every** Bash/Edit/Write call that targets a linked worktree, including read-only `git status`. `admit_session()` requires schema 2 and raised `explicit-schema-upgrade-required`; the plugin hid that reason behind `BLOCKED: lifecycle owner admission is unavailable; no write authorized`. Interactive sessions therefore had no checkout where both Bash and Edit worked, and workers dispatched for this issue failed before launch.

This PR takes option 2 from the issue: session admission follows the schema-1 compatibility rule that `worktree_create_registered` already uses (`--allow-schema-1-observation`).

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-session-helper.py` — `admit_targets()` calls `GenerationEnrollment.has_schema_one_gap()` for each root. A valid, unmarked schema-1 store returns `coverage-gap` and prints `coverage-gap: schema-upgrade-required` to stderr. No owner is admitted, no marker is published, the store is not migrated, and `cleanup_authorized` stays false. Contradictory schema-1 state (a marker or an admission table) still refuses. Refusals now include `detail` (the error message).
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/lifecycle-admission.mjs` — accepts `coverage-gap`. The BLOCKED message now names the helper reason, e.g. `(StoreConflict: schema-one-with-admission-state)`.
- `.agents/hooks/git_safety_lifecycle.py` — accepts `coverage-gap` (Claude Code guard).
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/CLEANUP.md` — documents the behaviour under "Interactive tool admission".

Out of scope: a coordinated `upgrade-schema` command (option 1). Older running clients (v3.39.57–v3.39.107 were live on the reporting host) still reject schema 2, so a migration needs its own coordination.

## Verification

- Reproduction on a disposable repo, linked worktree and lifecycle store, calling the helper directly:
  - `main`, schema 1: exit 75, `{"status": "unavailable", "reason": "ValueError"}`
  - this branch, schema 1: exit 0, `coverage-gap`, `user_version` still 1, no generation marker
  - this branch, schema 2: `admitted`, marker published (unchanged)
  - this branch, schema 1 with an admission table: exit 75, `StoreConflict: schema-one-with-admission-state` (still fails closed)
- `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-git-safety-gate.mjs`: 30/30 pass. This includes the closed-generation rejections and the Claude hook path.
- `python3 -m unittest tests.test_enrollment tests.test_admission tests.test_admitted_launch` (in `.agents/worker-lifecycle`): 64 OK, 2 skipped.
- `node --check lifecycle-admission.mjs`: OK.

Running sessions pick this up only after deploy (`setup.sh` / `aidevops update`) and a new runtime session, because the plugin runs from its runtime bundle.

Resolves #36349

Accept confirmed worktree disappearance as an explicit terminal registry outcome, without claiming successful preservation. Fix Pulse reporting so missing sources and generic cleanup errors are not counted as archive failures.

## Cause and implementation

Admissions can survive interrupted creation or removal outside the retirement executor. Previously, cleanup repeatedly attempted to inspect the missing source, retained the admission, and Pulse reported all failures as archive failures.

- Add `worker_lifecycle/absence.py`: use the existing generation lock and an admission writer transaction to journal `worktree-absence-reconciled` and release only that generation's admission.
- Record `source-disappeared` or `creation-unconfirmed`, always with `preservation=unverified` and `cleanup_authorized=false`. Retain generation, binding, run and event history. No files or Git administration are removed, and no new database/schema is introduced.
- Require an accessible, unchanged parent and confirmed source absence. Live/unknown owners, competing admissions, replacements, permission errors and incomplete private relocation remain blocked or retryable. Planned retirement resumes through the existing executor.
- Update `cleanup.py`, `legacy_cleanup.py` and `pulse-cleanup-worktree-removal.sh` to distinguish retired, reconciled, held, failed and actual archive-helper failures. Diagnostics omit raw command arguments/stdout/stderr.
- Document the contract in `ABSENCE.md`; include the new implementation and tests in the portable validation bundle.

Reference patterns: existing generation retirement locks, `DirectoryHandle`, admission transactions and immutable journal events. The separate merge `FETCH_HEAD` archive limitation is not changed by this PR.

## Verification

- Scoped regression: 55 tests passed across absence, retirement, admission recovery, legacy cleanup, launcher integration and portable bundle.
- After adding present-directory/missing-Git-metadata coverage and exercising reconciliation through the real Pulse shell adapter: 22 tests passed in `tests.test_absence` and `tests.test_launcher_paths`.
- Ruff 0.11.13, mypy 1.15.0 for Linux and Darwin targets, ShellCheck, scoped Bandit 1.8.6, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Pre-commit hooks passed. Native macOS execution has not been performed for this change; Darwin mypy is only static verification.
- Local Qlty execution was unavailable because its executable is not installed; no passing Qlty result is claimed.
- Pre-push hooks allowed the push, explicitly deferring the root JavaScript typecheck to CI because local `tsc`/dev dependencies are absent. That typecheck has not passed locally.

Reproduce the focused runtime checks from the repository root:

```sh
PYTHONPATH=.agents/worker-lifecycle python3 -B -m unittest tests.test_absence tests.test_launcher_paths -q
```

Tests cover ended/live/unknown owners, empty reservations, competing admission, replacement paths, absent parents, permission failures, transaction rollback, idempotent replay/path reuse, safe diagnostics and Pulse counters. Production registry data was not modified to test this fix.

title: GH#36378: fix runtime rollback after convergence failure
body:
## Summary
- Add lock-protected rollback of the candidate runtime link and deployed stamp after convergence failure.
- Preserve exact activation ownership across the CLI setup subprocess using a private receipt; do not undo concurrent deployments.
- Scope: `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/agent-deploy.sh`, `setup.sh`, `aidevops.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-aidevops-update-transaction.sh`.

Resolves #36378

## Runtime Testing
- **Risk**: High
- **Verification**: runtime-verified — executed the existing `run_activation_stamp_test` fixture and extraction helpers directly from the updated transaction test: 1 passed, 0 failed. Assertions cover setup and CLI convergence failures with distinct candidate/baseline SHAs, successful verification, concurrent activation preservation, receipt-write failure, and first-install rollback without a previous stamp.
- `bash -n` passes for all four changed shell files; `git diff --check` passes; repository commit hooks pass.
- Full `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-aidevops-update-transaction.sh` was attempted: its first eight checks pass, then existing Git integration fixtures cannot run because they hard-code `/usr/bin/git`, absent on this Nix runner. Git itself is available elsewhere. No claim of a complete suite pass.
- Local ShellCheck wrapper has no real binary; CI `cross-platform-shellcheck` covers it. Push hook reports unavailable TypeScript dependencies and defers typecheck to CI; no TypeScript changes.

## Review
Independent focused review found no unconditional correctness defect. The conditional root-reuse concern does not apply to ordinary setup staging: `_runtime_bundle_stage` allocates a fresh `mktemp` bundle directory per deployment. Rollback matches the existing exact-root ownership guard and never infers candidate ownership from a post-setup link observation. The review-evidence bundler could not run because the runner lacks `file`; direct diff inspection and supplied-source review were used instead.

## Implementation notes
The CLI uses a private temporary receipt because setup runs in a subprocess; activation records candidate root, previous root, and previous stamp while holding the transition lock. Both recovery callers use the lock-protected helper, which restores the stamp through `_runtime_bundle_restore_stamp` only when it still owns the active candidate. Receipt contents are read as data, never sourced as shell code.

title: GH#36390: fail fast when worker spawn never submits (circuit-breaker trip #36389 root cause)
body:
## Summary

Root cause of supervisor circuit-breaker trip Ref #36389: on the tripping runner, five consecutive dispatches (2026-11-01 18:25–18:30Z, one pulse process, including awardsapp#12414) posted `Dispatching worker` with an empty **Worker PID** right after `opencode_warm_done`. No `[systemd-launch]` sidecar lines were appended, so the failure happened before a systemd unit was submitted. `_dlw_nohup_launch` ended with `_dlw_exec_detached ...; return 0`, which swallowed that spawn failure. Launch validation then waited ~60s, found no process and recorded `no_worker_process`, and three of those tripped the breaker.

Fix in `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh` (new `_dlw_spawn_worker_or_fail`):
- Clear the per-worker `.systemd-launch` sidecar before spawning, so a missing sidecar now means "no unit was submitted".
- No unit submitted, or no numeric PID: return 1. The existing `worker_launch_failed` path then rolls back ownership and posts no fake dispatch comment. A `worker_spawn_failed` lifecycle line goes to the worker log, the backend error goes to the pulse log, and `worker_spawn_failed` is recorded in the supervisor breaker, so systemic spawn breakage still pauses dispatch, now with an accurate reason.
- Unit submitted but readiness unconfirmed: keep the old handoff, so launch validation still decides by process scan. This matches `reference/pulse-runtime-contracts.md`: an ambiguous response does not prove the worker is absent.

The backend-specific cause on the tripping runner, most likely an unreachable systemd user manager or a failed managed-lifetime reserve, is only in that runner's local pulse log. After this change it shows up directly as `worker_spawn_failed` instead of being hidden.

## Files Changed

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh`: fix
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-spawn-fail-fast.sh`: new regression guard (same pattern as `test-prelaunch-publication-reserve.sh`)

## Decisions

Unit-submitted-but-unconfirmed keeps the legacy launch-validation handoff to avoid duplicate workers (pulse-runtime-contracts.md). Supervisor breaker now records worker_spawn_failed for definite spawn failures so systemic breakage still pauses dispatch.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Medium
- **Verification:** runtime-verified

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-spawn-fail-fast.sh`: 5/5 pass. It runs the real `_dlw_spawn_worker_or_fail` with only the backend and breaker stubbed, and covers:

title: t18848: docs(hostinger): installed package release without rpm, Red Hat VEX source, ImageMagick advisories, account policy test
body:
## Summary

Updates the "Read-only audit notes" in `.agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md` so the next image-library advisory check can tell, without waiting for support, whether a shared host's package is fixed.

- **Installed package release without `rpm`** (new): each binary's `.gnu_debuglink` names its package version-release on RHEL 8+ builds. Use `readelf --string-dump=.gnu_debuglink`, or a `grep -ao` fallback.
- **Ghostscript fix status**: read Red Hat's VEX JSON (one file per CVE), not the CVE page. The page's package table needs JavaScript, and its Statement still said "under analysis" after the fix shipped.
- **Which advisories apply** (new): ImageMagick's GitHub security advisories list each affected range.
- **Security policy**: the account-level `MAGICK_CONFIGURE_PATH` policy that support suggested does not reach website `lsphp` workers. `putenv()` is too late, and a `PDF:` prefix still sends PostScript to Ghostscript.
- **Libraries without `ldd`**: CloudLinux's `imagick.so` contains ImageMagick statically, so match `imagick.so`, not `libMagick`.
- **Missing commands**: `ldd`, `readelf`, `objdump`, `strings` and `file` were on PATH on 2026-11-02.

## Evidence

All read-only, on one Hostinger Cloud account (CloudLinux 8), 2026-11-01 and 2026-11-02 UTC:

- `readelf --string-dump=.gnu_debuglink /usr/bin/gs` printed `gs-9.27-19.el8_10.x86_64.debug`. Red Hat's VEX file lists `ghostscript-9.27-19.el8_10` as RHEL 8's fix for CVE-2026-101258 (RHSA-2026:83552), so the host carried the fix. Support's reply had left the package name blank.
- The ImageMagick advisories API returned 21 advisories published 2026-11-01 (8 medium, 13 low) affecting versions below 7.1.2-35. The host and CloudLinux's newest `alt-ImageMagick` were on 7.1.2-34.
- Every command added to the doc was run as written: the VEX `curl | jq`, the advisories `gh api`, and `readelf`/`grep` over SSH.

## Verification

- `markdownlint .agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md`: no findings.
- `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD`: `hostinger.md` and this task's `TODO.md` entry only.
- No private site names, account identifiers or local paths are added.

Resolves #36439

title: t18849: fix .archive-verify-* and .restore-* scratch leaks (GH#36468)
body:
## Summary

`.archive-verify-*` scratch copies (~300M each) piled up beside recovery archives at roughly 10–15G/day. This PR fixes why they leak, not only the leftover directories.

### Root cause

1. `verify_in_scratch` removed its scratch copy only on success. Its callers stopped it with SIGKILL on timeout (`preservation.py` after 120 s, `worktree_archive_prune.py` after 60 s), so every killed check left a full copy behind.
2. `prune` ran a full `verify` (~57 s each; the base import takes most of that) on **every** archive before it chose what to delete, even in dry-run. It could never finish within `timeout_sec 120` in `cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh`, so every pass ended with `rc=124` and left one more copy.
3. Since GH#36281 the scratch name was derived from the archive alone. One killed check therefore blocked every later check of that archive (`archive-verify:retained-scratch`).
4. The same leak exists in producer transactions. A restoration proof that died or failed after `.creation.json` but before comparison stayed in state `restoring`. `RestorationProof.cleanup` refused that slot on every retry, so the full registered worktree under `.producer-transactions/<id>/.restore-*` stayed forever. The timing log shows 2195 `canonical-restore` starts against 2155 successful cleanups.

### Fix

- **Scratch lifetime has a live owner** (new `worktree_archive_scratch.py`):
  - Each check gets its own `mkdtemp` directory, `.archive-verify-<sha256(archive)>-<rand>`, and holds an exclusive `flock` on it.
  - A directory whose lock nobody holds belongs to a dead check. It is swept after a 600 s grace period.
  - Success and cancellation (KeyboardInterrupt/SIGTERM) remove the directory.
  - A real verification failure keeps only the newest copy per archive as evidence, with a `.aidevops-verify-failed` marker, for 24 h (`AIDEVOPS_WORKTREE_VERIFY_EVIDENCE_TTL_HOURS`; 0 disables).
- **Interruption is cooperative.** Callers send SIGTERM to the process group, wait 10 s, then send SIGKILL (`run_bounded`, `preservation.py` `_run`), so cleanup code actually runs.
- **Prune fits its budget:**
  - It selects archives by metadata and verifies only the ones it is about to delete.
  - It works within `--budget-seconds` / `AIDEVOPS_WORKTREE_ARCHIVE_PRUNE_BUDGET` (default 540 s). Archives it can't reach are reported as `deferred`, which is not an error.
  - The async cleanup sweeps dead scratch first (60 s, in every retention mode including `off`), then runs prune with `timeout_sec` = budget + 60.
- **Restore slots can be reclaimed.** Under the operation lock, a sealed but never-compared slot is adopted from its `.creation.json`: slot and target inodes must match, and cleanup still requires the current registration and owner to equal the sealed ones. Only the content comparison is skipped. A transferred or changed owner is still retained.
- New subcommand `worktree-archive-helper.sh sweep-scratch`.

### Why this fixes the cause and not the symptom

Deleting old directories on a schedule would only hide the leak and could delete a copy that is still in use. Here the directory's lifetime is tied to a live process (the flock), cancellation cleans up deterministically, and the job that kept being killed now finishes within its time limit. Orphans can still appear after a crash or power loss, and the sweep removes those once their owner is provably dead.

### Out of scope

Retention for `.producer-archives` is tracked separately in #36470 (t18850).

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-cleanup-worktrees-async.sh`: 39/39
- `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-archive-lifecycle.py -k pack_failure -k scratch -k prune -k pin -k retention -k terminated -k canonical`: 43/43 OK (after the qlty refactor; an earlier run including unsealed/unregistered cases gave 39/39 OK)
- worker-lifecycle unittest (CI command, `umask 022`): 233/233 OK. Under a group-writable umask 002 the existing fixtures are rejected by design (`unsafe-repository-config`); that is unrelated to this PR.
- `qlty smells` on the changed modules: no smells. Process control was moved into `worktree_archive_process.py`, and `sweep`/`prune` were split to stay under complexity and parameter limits.
- ShellCheck clean; pre-commit passed

Resolves #36468

title: t18858: accept owner-private-group archive chains on umask 002 hosts (GH#36490)
body:
## Summary

Registry retirement refused **every** worktree on Ubuntu/Debian hosts that use user-private groups (`USERGROUPS_ENAB yes`, so the effective umask is 002). Archive roots created there are `0775`, and `worker_lifecycle/filesystem.py:_check_directory` rejected any group-writable directory in the chain:

```json
{"reason": "archive-path-externally-writable", "filesystem_path": "~/.aidevops/recovery", "status": "unavailable"}
```

Observed impact on one host:

- 48 retained `<profile>-profile-readme-*` worktrees and hundreds of failed `aidevops-worker-session-*` cleanup units.
- Each hourly profile publication re-archived and re-verified its worktree through the fallback path and still could not remove it. This produced 2569 of the 2991 recorded `producer-validation` runs.
- Pulse logged "Observation-era cleanup unavailable: archive-path-externally-writable".

The rejected group was the owner's private group (uid = gid = 1000, group named after the user, no members), and `~/.aidevops` was `0700`. No other principal could write anywhere in the chain, so the refusal was a false positive. GH#36465 only made *new* lifecycle-subprocess directories private. Existing roots, the shell producer and the Python `mkdir(parents=True)` callers were unchanged, so the refusal persisted on 3.39.112.

## Changes

- `worker_lifecycle/filesystem.py`: group write is accepted only when no other principal can use it:
  - the directory's group is the owner's **user-private group** (the same rule enrollment already applies to Git admin dirs since GH#36142), or
  - it lies **below an owned directory that others cannot search** (`mode & 0o011 == 0`).

  Both exceptions require a Linux directory without an extended access ACL. Other write is still always rejected, and archive leaves still require `0700`. The existing enrollment helpers moved here, so both validators share one rule; `enrollment.py` keeps thin wrappers, so existing patches still work.
- `worker_lifecycle/archive_path.py`: new `create_archive_root` creates each missing component `0700`. `Path.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True)` gave parents `0777 & ~umask`. It is used by `cleanup.py` (targeted and pass) and `legacy_cleanup.py`.
- `audit-worktree-removal-helper.sh`: create the producer root under `umask 077`.
- `worker-lifecycle-state.sh`: on refusal, print `[worker-lifecycle] retirement-refused status=… reason=… path=…` to stderr instead of discarding the registry result. Only the controlled fields are printed, never raw output.

Existing directories are never modified (no chmod), consistent with GH#36361 and GH#36465.

## Why this fixes the cause

The refusal came from the validator misclassifying a private group as external. The validator now recognises the two cases where group write cannot be used by anyone else. That is the convention the OS itself relies on when it sets umask 002 for user-private-group users. Shared groups, other-writable directories and ACL-bearing directories stay rejected.

## Verification

- `.agents/worker-lifecycle`: `python3 -E -s -B -m unittest discover -s tests` under umask 022 → **Ran 235 tests, OK**. New cases in `tests/test_filesystem.py`:
  - shared group rejected, ACL present rejected, private group accepted;
  - sealed ancestor accepted, `0777` under a sealed ancestor rejected;
  - umask-002 root creation yields `0700` and leaves existing modes unchanged.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-managed-lifetime.py` → 25 OK (2 skipped).
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-removal-audit-lib.sh` → 71/72. `snapshot_backend_requires_visible_target` fails identically on `main` (`8a08e47be`); it is a host process-cwd test and unrelated to this change.
- `linters-local.sh --changed`: ShellCheck, secretlint and whitespace pass. The two shfmt advisories are pre-existing lines.
- Live host, read-only: `validate_archive_path(~/.aidevops/recovery/archives)` → deployed code `refused archive-path-externally-writable ~/.aidevops/recovery`; this branch `accepted`.

Resolves #36490

title: t18851: compact-archive prune uses structural checks, not full verify (GH#36479)
body:
## Summary

Compact-archive retention (`worktree_archive_prune.py`) ran a **full** `worktree-archive-helper.sh verify` on every archive selected for expiry. A full verify imports the base objects and checks restorability. Restorability does not affect whether an expired archive may be deleted: a broken archive loses nothing by expiring. So the check cost a lot of time and bought no safety, and it was the main reason prune passes timed out (`rc=124`, GH#36468).

What retention does need is **identity**: the directory must be an intact compact archive and never a full recovery copy (`worktree-archive-helper.md` "Full recovery copies are a separate store"), must not be pinned, and must not have changed since selection.

## Changes

- `worktree-archive-helper.sh`: new `verify-structure ARCHIVE_DIR` mode. It runs the existing first stage of `verify` and stops before the Git object import:
  - schema;
  - exact artifact inventory with mandatory artifacts;
  - directory contents equal to that inventory;
  - no symlinks;
  - sizes and sha256.

  Full recovery copies and tampered archives still fail and are kept.
- `worktree_archive_prune.py`: call `verify-structure`. The per-check budget is now 120 s with a 10 s minimum, replacing the base-import timeout + 300 s and the 60 s minimum. The pin, manifest, directory-identity and no-follow `.prune-<id>` claim checks are unchanged, both before and after the check.
- `worktree-archive-helper.md`: document the retention check.

## Measurement (one real host archive)

| check | rc | seconds |
|---|---:|---:|
| `verify-structure` | 0 | 0.46 |
| `verify` (full) | 0 | 82.54 |

## Verification

- `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-archive-lifecycle.py -k prune -k pin -k retention -k scratch` → 29 of 30 pass. These include the existing retention preview/apply, age/size, pin, pin-during-check and unsafe/corrupt archive cases.
- The one error, and both `-k migrat` errors, are 60 s `worktree-recovery-lifecycle-helper.sh compact` timeouts in migration tests that do not call prune. The same two tests fail identically on the pre-change tree (`9cf4f6dbc`) on the same host, at load average 83.
- `shellcheck -x .agents/scripts/worktree-archive-helper.sh` → clean.

## Regression Evidence

This PR changes no test files. Coverage comes from the existing retention cases in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-archive-lifecycle-cases.py`: pinned, symlinked, corrupt, unknown-content and changed-during-check archives are kept, and age/size selection still applies. All of them now run through `verify-structure`. `test_pin_added_during_verification_preserves_claimed_archive` patches `module.verify` and still passes.

Resolves #36479

title: GH#36504: compact worktree deletion archive payloads
body:
## Summary

Resolves #36504.

Store deleted paths as staged/unstaged path, mode and blob-ID records instead of copying deleted contents into patches. Preserve other patch changes, ignored-file exclusion, literal byte-preserving paths, old archive reading, and the existing fingerprint contract.

The implementation is in `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_deletions.py`, integrated through `worktree-archive-helper.sh` capture/restore and `worktree_archive_local_verify.py`. Portable bundle sources and `CLEANUP.md` document the extension.

## Evidence

A deletion-only patch covering 8,652 paths occupied 147,168,550 bytes. Encoding those same deletion identities produces 1,316,193 bytes (about 112 times smaller). This is a payload representation measurement, not a production archive migration or cleanup throughput claim.

## Runtime Testing

- `PYTHONPATH=.agents/worker-lifecycle python3 -B -m unittest tests.test_preservation tests.test_local_archive_verification tests.test_retirement`: 36 tests passed on Linux before and after rebasing onto current main; the repeated run completed in 326.697 seconds.

## Risk and limitations

Risk level: medium. Testing level: runtime-verified.

This changes archive payload capture and restoration. Local verification reconstructs full diffs in memory to preserve existing fingerprint semantics, so CPU/memory costs are not eliminated. title: t18850: evidence-based expiry for producer recovery archives (GH#36470)
body:
## Summary

Producer recovery archives (`<root>/.producer-archives/<id>/<owner>__<repo>/unattributed/<ts>/`) were pinned with "no automatic expiry authority", and compact retention never looked at them. Every removal of an unattributed worktree therefore left a permanent archive. Hourly profile-readme routines produced one each hour until the operator deleted `recovery/archives` by hand.

This PR gives them an **evidence-based** lifetime. It is the cause-level fix: the pin now has an end condition, and an archive that preserves nothing (an empty delta) no longer lives forever.

## Evidence (host, before change)

All 4 producer archives created since the manual cleanup, 14:47Z–17:48Z, are empty deltas: `head_sha == base_sha`, `dirty_state: clean`, and `diff.patch`, `staged.patch` and `untracked-files.txt` are 0 bytes. Their journals say `source_removal_outcome: pending` even though the worktrees are gone, because they were retired by another path.

## Changes

- New `worktree_archive_producer_retention.py`. A producer archive is eligible only when **all** of these hold:
  - the journal matches the archive (path + manifest sha256) and records a completed capture (`archived`; `verified` for legacy receipts);
  - the recorded source path **and** its Git admin dir no longer exist (`removed`, or `pending` with both observed absent; the same evidence `check(removed=True)` records);
  - there is no `.keep` in the archive.
- Empty delta (HEAD at base, clean, only zero-byte patches/inventory): expires at the next apply pass.
- Any other producer archive: expires `--producer-ttl-days` after capture (default 30, `AIDEVOPS_WORKTREE_PRODUCER_ARCHIVE_TTL_DAYS`).
- `worktree_archive_prune.py`: adds the eligible producer entries. The size cap counts protected producer bytes but never removes them. `remove_verified` requires the exact producer pin bytes and no `.keep`, both before claiming and after the structural check.
- Apply re-checks the evidence under the producer `operation_lock`, removes through the existing claimed transaction, retires `.producer-transactions/<id>/`, and removes the empty `.producer-archives/<id>/…` parents.
- `worktree-archive-helper.sh` gets `--producer-ttl-days`. `cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh` passes the env value.
- Docs: `worktree-archive-helper.md` ("Retention", producer listing note) and `dirty-worktree-preservation.md`.
- `TODO.md`: records the completed t18851 (#36503), which was missing.

Retention mode is unchanged. The default stays `dry-run`; apply still needs `storage.worktree_archive_retention_mode: "apply"`.

### Deliberate deviation from the issue: capture stays archive-first

The issue suggested creating **no** archive for an empty delta. This PR does not. All four callers of `archive_worktree_path_recoverably` hand the archive to `remove_archived_worktree_path`, which runs `source-matches` against the recorded fingerprint right before native removal. The archive is that removal's identity proof. An empty archive is about 150 KB and now expires at the next pass, so the storage outcome is the same without weakening a destructive path. Details: https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/36470#issuecomment-6587902270

## Verification

- Host dry-run with this branch (`prune --dry-run --output-root ~/.aidevops/recovery/archives`): all 4 archives report `producer-eligible … empty-delta` and pass `verify-structure`; nothing is removed.
- New case `test_prune_expires_producer_archive_only_on_evidence` (in the existing `worktree_recovery_producer_cases.py`, run by `test-worktree-archive-lifecycle.py`) checks four states:
  1. Source present: kept, even with a 1K cap.
  2. `.keep` present: kept.
  3. `--dry-run`: reports `empty-delta` and keeps the archive.
  4. `--apply`: removes the archive, its journal directory and the empty producer parents.
- `-k prune -k pin -k retention -k producer_transaction`: 9 tests OK.
- `shellcheck -x` clean on both changed shell scripts.

## Regression Evidence

The changed test file is `.agents/scripts/tests/worktree_recovery_producer_cases.py`. The new case covers the defect: before this change `candidate_entries()` only globbed `*/*/*/manifest.json` and `inspect()` refused every pinned archive, so `prune --apply` could never remove a producer archive whose source was gone. The host dry-run above is the live reproduction: the 4 archives are now selected, and before this change they were invisible.

Resolves #36470

title: GH#36494: routine-created worktrees become retirable; remove refusals name cause and next step
body:
## Summary

Implements the approved review plan (options B/C/D; A and E rejected). 1) Provenance: pulse-routines.sh _routine_declare_lifecycle_owner makes the detached script-routine runner declare AIDEVOPS_LIFECYCLE_RUNTIME_PID/SESSION_ID (replacing any inherited identity; cleared when lifecycle is disabled/private/unavailable). Helper worktrees (e.g. badges sync) then get controlled creation owned by the runner, which waits for the script; once it exits, the registry cleanup pass archives and retires them. 2) Actionable refusals: cleanup-worktree maps a linked tree whose Git admin dir has no enrollment marker to detail=not-enrolled (missing sources and damaged markers keep their errors), reports mode=retirement, and code-shaped ValueError causes are surfaced via refusal.py. worker_lifecycle_cleanup_worktree names every local prerequisite refusal (lifecycle-disabled, jq/python3-unavailable, registry-state-unavailable) instead of returning silently, and includes detail in the refusal line. 3) Operator path: manual worktree-helper.sh remove prints the next step per cause; not-enrolled prints the existing archive-first, operator-confirmed worker-legacy-cleanup.py --confirm-legacy-path command (preview; --apply archives, verifies, removes, keeps branches). Next-step text is only printed for explicit operator requests, so per-cycle Pulse cleanup logs stay one line per tree. Docs: CLEANUP.md, commands/worktree-cleanup.md.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh, .agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-state.sh, .agents/scripts/worktree-helper-cmds.sh, .agents/worker-lifecycle/CLEANUP.md, .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/cleanup.py, .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/refusal.py, .agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/registry.py, .agents/workflows/worktree-cleanup.md

## Decisions

Option A (regenerable class bypassing the registry) and E (wall-clock idle) are not implemented, per the review: single registry authority and boot-bound idle stay intact. title: fix(worktrees): drain pulse unit launches whose recorded boot has ended
body:
## Summary

Pulse-managed worktrees whose last worker launch was recorded in a **previous boot** could never be sealed, so `worktree-helper.sh clean` skipped them forever with `managed-worktree: ValueError: boot generation unavailable` → `cleanup lease was not acquired`. The idle path had the same dead end (`idle boot generation unavailable`). On an affected host this left merged worktrees pinned while the disk reached 99%.

A reboot terminates every process of the recorded boot, which is stronger descendant evidence than sampling a unit. The owner-observation path already accepts this (`previous-boot-ended` in `worktree_lifetime_quiescence.py`); pulse unit launches did not.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/worktree_lifetime_owner.py`: `drain_unit()` issues a `previous-boot-ended` receipt when both the recorded and current boot IDs are valid UUIDs and differ, and the launch has a bound invocation. Unit/cgroup state is deliberately not sampled across boots (names and cgroup paths can be reused). Added `previous_boot_receipt_valid()`.
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_lifetime_proof.py`: `proof()` accepts a validated previous-boot receipt in place of a systemd snapshot; forged receipts (same boot, mismatched invocation) are rejected.
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_lifetime_idle.py`: idle quiescence routes prior-boot launches through `drain()` instead of raising. The idle interval is still boot-bound via `interval_valid`, so the window restarts after reboot.
- Tests: `tests/test-worktree-owner-lifetime.py` covers the ended-boot receipt, proof acceptance, forged-receipt rejection, and unbound prior-boot admission refusal.

## Verification

- `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-owner-lifetime.py` — 29 OK
- `test-worktree-managed-lifetime.py`, `test-worktree-managed-run.py`, `test-worktree-owner-native.py`, `test-worktree-process-census.py`, `test-worktree-seal-observed.py` — OK
- `test-worktree-add-managed-symlink-base.sh` / `test-precreation-failure-skip.sh` fail identically on unmodified code on this host because the disk-capacity guard refuses worktree creation (environmental).
- Live: a merged worktree with a prior-boot launch (`state: running`) failed `worktree-managed-lifetime.py seal` with `boot generation unavailable` before this change.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Worktree cleanup now handles launches from a previous system boot using their recorded completion receipt, without relying on unavailable system service evidence.
  * Idle waiting restarts its observation window for prior-boot launches.
  * Receipts with invalid boot details or mismatched launch information continue to be rejected.
  * Archive validation now accepts file and directory permissions allowed by the current process umask, while retaining existing ownership and metadata checks.

title: GH#36525: triage unknown blocked checkpoints
body:
## Summary

Resolves #36525.

Classify unknown terminal blockers on the releasing runner, then route positively identified pending work through the existing revision-bound continuation approval path. Ownership, permission, scope, protected-label, brief and exact-head safeguards remain in force.

- Run one bounded, inference-only triage over protected final-assistant evidence. Known prerequisites retain their normal blocker class/owner; ambiguous, truncated or unavailable evidence remains held. Missing Files Scope stays a structural check, not an inferred class.
- Bind pending-work eligibility to the exact decoded issue body SHA-256 and worktree HEAD. Repo policy defaults off. Automatic approval requires current write authority for the configured policy owner, publishing actor and releasing runner, plus fresh target/template validation.
- Without the policy, elect one daily digest publisher through atomic creation of an **unassigned** `checkpoint-digest:YYYY-MM-DD` label. Publish one immutable, bounded snapshot of validated approval-template commands; do not race indexed search or competing comment updates.
- Expose observed unknown triage backlog, oldest trusted release age and unreadable/unscanned count in Pulse health.

### Files

- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`: bounded private-evidence triage.
- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`: policy and guarded routing.
- `.agents/reference/checkpoint-revision-recovery.md`: operator contract.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-check-queue-scan.py` and `pulse-check-helper.sh`: bounded health collection and rendering.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse_check_checkpoints.py`: focused trusted-release health module, following the existing dependencies/progress module pattern.
- Existing terminal-blocker and continuation test entrypoints: focused classification, policy and concurrent-digest coverage.

## Runtime Testing

Risk: **high**. Testing level: **runtime-verified** through the existing isolated CLI suites (GitHub/inference transports are stubbed; no live continuation policy or approvals were enabled).

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`: **56 passed**, 0 failed.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`: **153 passed**, including the existing embedded Python suites for revision/claim/private-member/self-hold checks.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-check-helper.sh`: **203 passed**, 0 failed.
- ShellCheck **0.11.0**: zero findings across all five changed shell files. The normal PATH wrapper initially failed to find its binary; the installed system binary was discovered with `type -a shellcheck` and used directly.
- Bash syntax, Python compilation and `git diff --check`: pass.
- Direct scanner fixture: a verified-write runner's release is measured as **1,440 minutes** old, edited evidence is excluded, and unavailable comment reads increment the unreadable counter.
- After the quality-driven module extraction, nine direct runtime scenarios passed: trusted writer, edited evidence, read-only collaborator, mismatched runner, later claim, unreadable comments, invalid date, future date and empty history. The existing Pulse suite was rerun for the refactor.
- The repository push hook cannot start root `bun run typecheck` because local JavaScript development dependencies / `tsc` are absent; it explicitly defers this check to default-branch CI. No Node/TypeScript files changed.
- Initial exact-head Qlty / CodeFactor failures identified collector and main-function complexity. The collector is now split into focused module helpers and optional history enrichment is outside `main`; no quality configuration, baseline or threshold changed. Local Qlty CLI is unavailable, so CI owns the final static verdict.

## Acceptance review

| Criterion | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Pending work distinguished from real prerequisites | Production triage parser exercised with pending-only, dependency, permission, input-owner, scope-exclusion, source-access and runner-prerequisite decisions; malformed/conflicting results stay held |
| Policy off: one daily digest, no approval | Concurrent writers compete for one native reservation; test observes exactly one immutable snapshot and no approval declaration |
| Policy on: trusted approval path, existing rejection guards | Fixture invokes the signed-wrapper publication boundary; claimed owner, no-auto-dispatch, moved head, insufficient write permission and failed template validation reject; existing continuation/revision suites remain green |
| Triage age visible without inventing fleet completeness | Direct age/trust/unreadable fixture and full Pulse health suite pass; report labels observations as bounded |

Two independent advisory review passes examined the changed production paths. Findings addressed: untrusted approval-looking comments no longer suppress publication (reuse authoritative revision validation); exact-byte brief hashing preserves trailing newlines; atomic daily reservation plus immutable snapshot eliminates digest creation/update races; inferred missing-scope results cannot bypass structural verification.

## Operational decisions

- A daily snapshot examines at most 100 blocked auto-dispatch issues / 100 worker drafts with a 40-second enrichment budget. Later or unreadable candidates enter the next UTC snapshot. Reservations remain as audit records and are never attached to issues.
- A reservation whose publication outcome is ambiguous is not retried that day: at-most-once publication takes precedence over duplicate notifications. The next day's snapshot can recover the still-pending candidate.
- Existing legacy releases without runner-produced eligibility evidence are not promoted from PR-body prose. Their unknown age remains visible for protected-evidence recovery.
- Policy stays off unless an operator configures it. This PR changes no live repo policy, permissions, credentials, assignments or protective labels. Release/deployment is not requested.

title: fix: recognize fork-headed merged local branches (GH#36566)
body:
## Summary

Resolves #36566. For #36561 (child A only).

- Resolve the upstream base repository once when scanning a fork remote.
- Use branch upstream owner/ref for closed-PR evidence, including renamed local branches.
- Recognize local tips ancestral to merged PR heads only when the merged commit object is present locally.
- Preserve fail-closed lookup handling and bounded closed-PR request accounting.
- Never treat a fork's default-branch ancestry as proof of an upstream merge.

## Files and reference pattern

Implementation: `.agents/scripts/local-branch-cleanup-helper.sh`; focused fixtures: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-local-branch-cleanup-fork-pr.sh`; existing fixture metadata stub: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-local-branch-cleanup-helper.sh`. Follow the existing exact-SHA evidence path and local cleanup fixture style. The adjacent test update is recorded in the issue's canonical Files Scope.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/local-branch-cleanup-helper.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-local-branch-cleanup-fork-pr.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-local-branch-cleanup-helper.sh` — pass.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-local-branch-cleanup-fork-pr.sh` — pass: exact head, local ancestor, missing object, renamed upstream, fork remote, open PR, lookup/metadata failure, pagination failure, shared request cap, positive-evidence recheck, audited deletion and fork-only ancestry refusal.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-local-branch-cleanup-helper.sh` — pass: existing ancestry, squash, protection, active worktree, lease, transport cleanup and local-only behavior.
- `git diff --check` and commit hooks — pass.
- Push hook reports JavaScript development dependencies absent (`tsc` missing), deferring repository typecheck to existing CI. No TypeScript changes.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — both fixture suites execute the production cleanup helper, including guarded apply-mode deletion and refusal, on isolated Git repositories with stubbed GitHub responses. Commands above passed for pushed head `5e2309a4e`.

## Decisions

- Repository metadata is resolved once per scan, separate from the existing closed-PR lookup budget, just like the cached open-PR listing. Every closed-PR page and mutation-time recheck now shares that request cap.
- Ancestor proof never fetches missing objects; absent merged-head objects preserve the branch.
- Fork-selected scans require parent merged-PR evidence rather than fork-default ancestry.

Changelog

Sourced from github/codeql-action/upload-sarif's changelog.

CodeQL Action Changelog

See the releases page for the relevant changes to the CodeQL CLI and language packs.

[UNRELEASED]

No user facing changes.

4.39.2 - 03 Nov 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.4. #4284
  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.22.3 and earlier were discontinued on 16 October 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.18, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4266
  • Starting with macOS 27 and Xcode 27, traced analyses are unsupported. See this blog post for more information. The CodeQL Action will now try to identify if a workflow is about to perform a traced analysis on version 27 or above of macOS or Xcode. If so, the CodeQL Action will emit a corresponding warning that will also be visible on the Tool Status Page. This check will be rolled out following this release of the CodeQL Action. #4221
  • The undocumented TRAP cache cleanup feature that could be enabled using the CODEQL_ACTION_CLEANUP_TRAP_CACHES environment variable has been removed, as announced in the release notes for CodeQL Action 4.35.2. The analyze Action now warns if this environment variable is set. If you used TRAP cache cleanup to limit Actions cache usage, we recommend disabling TRAP caching by passing the trap-caching: false input to the init Action. #4243

4.39.1 - 21 Oct 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.3. #4256

4.39.0 - 15 Oct 2026

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. #4205
  • The codeql-action/analyze step now validates that a correct argument for the checkout_path input has been provided. The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. If the path does not point to a repository checkout or is different from the path that was used by codeql-action/init, then the CodeQL Action now produces a warning. #4148
  • Resolved an issue with third-party caching implementations that prevented caches from being restored correctly. #4206
  • The codeql-action/start-proxy step that is used in Code Scanning Default Setup now finds CodeQL releases using the same logic as codeql-action/init. This primarily benefits customers who are using GitHub instances other than github.com where the codeql-action/start-proxy step may previously have been unable to locate recent releases and ended up using outdated versions of the private registry authentication proxy as a result. #4198

4.38.3 - 08 Oct 2026

  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.21.2 and earlier were discontinued on 24 September 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.17, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4188
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.2. #4203
  • Fixed a bug where the decision of whether to use a per-language bundle did not account for custom configurations that reference queries outside of compiled CodeQL packs. This issue was caught during internal testing and did not affect any customer repositories. We will resume the roll out of per-language bundles in the coming weeks. #4184

4.38.2 - 24 Sept 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.1. #4160

4.38.1 - 18 Sept 2026

  • The CodeQL Action now has experimental support for CodeQL releases for which per-language bundles are available. Per-language bundles support analysis for a single language and are therefore smaller than the combined bundles that allow analysis for all supported languages. As a result, per-language bundles take up less space on disk and are faster to download. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in the coming weeks. #4146

4.38.0 - 09 Sept 2026

  • On GitHub-hosted runners, the CodeQL Action now deletes unused CodeQL bundles from the toolcache before downloading a different bundle, which frees up disk space for the analysis. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in September. #4124
  • The CodeQL Action now supports CodeQL releases that are compatible with Linux Arm64 and downloads the native linux-arm64 CodeQL bundle when available. #4072
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.0. #4129

4.37.9 - 26 Aug 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.4. #4106

Instead of editing the system prompt and busting the prompt cache, each change is added as a small update at the next step. The entries also survive compaction and reverts, and they don't start an extra model turn. (#56550)
  • Restored the Todo tool in desktop via opt-in (#59092)
  • Add configurable prompt cache TTLs per provider/model (#59157)

@opencode/ai root is now the Promise API

@opencode/ai now works like @opencode/sdk and @opencode/client: the package root exports the Promise API, and the Effect API moved to @opencode/ai/effect. @opencode/ai/promise is removed, and the wildcard subpath export is replaced with an explicit list of provider and protocol entry points. (#58847, #59183)

-import { AI } from "@opencode/ai/promise"
-import { LLM } from "@opencode/ai"
+import { AI } from "@opencode/ai"
+import { LLM } from "@opencode/ai/effect"

The OpenCode GitHub Action is removed

The OpenCode GitHub Action is no longer published. Remove it from your workflows. (#59032)

TUI plugins require OpenTUI 0.7

@opencode/plugin now requires @opentui/core and @opentui/solid 0.7.0, up from 0.6.8 or later. Plugins that depend on OpenTUI 0.6 fail to install until they upgrade. In OpenTUI 0.7, custom renderables read their hooks from their class at construction: assign renderBefore, renderAfter, and onLifecyclePass in the constructor instead of as class fields, call refreshHooks() after adding a hook by reflection, and replace defineNativeIntegration() with a static nativeIntegration declaration. title: GH#36595: fix(tabby): keep plain shells out of OpenCode recovery-marker directories
body:
Resolves #36595

## Root cause

Branch creation isn't the cause. Tabby-hosted OpenCode reports its private recovery-marker directory (`.../opencode-tabby-recovery/ses_<id>`) as the tab's cwd with `OSC 1337;CurrentDir`, so a crashed tab can restore the session. Tabby also uses that reported cwd for new tabs opened from the focused OpenCode tab. Plain interactive shells had no way to leave it. A restored plain tab then kept the marker as its process cwd, so the problem lasted across Tabby restarts. GH#32482 only covered typed OpenCode launches.

## Changes

- `.agents/scripts/tabby-recovery-shell-guard.sh` (new, sourced by interactive bash/zsh):
  - A shell that starts inside the recovery root moves to the marker's project `directory`, or to `$HOME` if the marker can't be used.
  - If the owner process is gone, it prints the resume command, deferred to precmd in zsh.
  - It skips `-c` command-string shells, so managed `-l -c 'exec aidevops opencode --tabby-shell'` profiles still restore.
  - Opt out with `AIDEVOPS_TABBY_MARKER_GUARD=0`.
- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/shell-env.sh`: `setup_tabby_recovery_shell_guard` adds one idempotent source line to the bash/zsh rc files.
- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/post-setup.sh`: `setup_tabby` calls the installer. It runs on setup, update and AI-session update, and only when Tabby is installed.
- `.agents/reference/tabby-profiles.md`: documents the behaviour.

## Verification

- Manual matrix with zsh 5.9, bash 5 and `/bin/bash` 3.2 (14/14 pass). Covered cases: live owner (silent move), dead owner (move plus V1/V2 hint), missing dir and marker root (`$HOME`), an unrelated dir, opt-out, and `zsh -i -c` / `bash -l -c` / non-interactive shells staying in the marker.
- Installer run twice on a scratch HOME: one block per rc file. `zsh -i` with the installed `.zshrc` lands in the project, and `zsh -l -c` stays in the marker.
- `shellcheck` clean; `tests/test-setup-scoped-dispatch.sh` 61/61; markdownlint clean.

title: GH#36564: fix: worktree archive capture checks capacity first and never retains failed captures (GH#36564)

## Summary

title: GH#36607: fix: published-worktree minimal archives, legacy preserve-v1 successor, linked branches dir, leaked-partial sweep
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #36564 (merged as #36609). Four approved preservation changes:

1. **Published-worktree minimal archive.** When HEAD differs from the base, no merge is in progress, and every commit since the base is reachable from a remote-tracking ref:
   - the manifest records `remote_branch_state: published`
   - no `commits.bundle` is written
   - the capacity estimate counts no commit payload

   `dependency_commit()` (`worktree_archive_objects.py`) makes snapshot seeding, local verification and restore depend on the published head, not the base. `verify-local` requires that head's complete graph and a remote-tracking ref, so removal is refused once the branch is gone. Restore imports a missing published head only through the existing explicitly authorized origin fetch, with no implicit network access. Unpushed work keeps the base-relative bundle (`unpublished`).
2. **Legacy `preserve-v1` reservations.** `reservation()` never resumes them. The source gets a stable git-only successor transaction, so the empty-directory, special-mode and capacity refusals are not re-armed. The legacy journal and archive stay in place for the existing retention, migration and retirement paths. The unused `preserve-v1` capture branch is removed.
3. **Admin `branches` entry.** An empty `branches` directory is accepted in linked admin dirs, as it already is in independent ones.
4. **`worktree-archive-helper.sh sweep-partials --dry-run|--apply [--output-root DIR]`.** A one-time cleanup of leaked partial captures. It takes each producer operation lock and skips busy locks. It then rechecks the phase (`reserved`/`capturing`), the directory and output inodes, and the source identity and head. Only exact-layout `<repo>/<issue>/<stamp>` directories with no manifest and no pin are listed or removed.

### Fixes needed to verify

- `_mark_failed` (`worktree_archive_scratch.py`) kept a fixed-format reason only if it had at most 300 characters after the prefix. `MISSING_PROMISOR_BASE` has 482, so the marker recorded only `ValueError`, and `test_missing_promisor_fails_closed_through_producer` has failed since GH#36468. The limit is now 600. The format check is unchanged, so markers still exclude raw stderr, paths and object IDs.
- GH#36504 (compact deletions) merged to `main` during this work. `test_git_only_capture_contains_commits_and_two_patches_without_verification` still expected deletion hunks in `staged.patch`. It now checks the compact-v1 payload and still runs the full restore round trip.

### Tests changed on purpose

- `test_producer_preserves_partial_capture_and_serializes_retry` now checks the sweep behaviour:
  - a retry never reallocates over a partial
  - dry-run keeps the partial
  - a held lock skips it
  - apply removes it
  - a later retry then captures normally
- `test_legacy_branches_requires_empty_independent_directory` follows item 3.
- New: a published-archive helper test and a legacy-successor producer test.

## Testing (Linux)

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-archive-helper.sh`: 10 tests, 0 failures.
- `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-archive-lifecycle.py`: 174 tests. The only remaining failures are the 5 prune cases tracked by #36613: 4 subtests of `test_corrupt_and_unknown_archives_are_preserved`, plus `test_symlinked_artifact_is_rejected`. They fail the same way on clean `main`. The promisor and git-only capture tests are fixed here and pass in targeted reruns.
- End-to-end producer fixture (bare origin, pushed 3-commit branch, empty ignored dir):
  - manifest has `remote_branch_state=published` and no `commits.bundle`
  - producer `verify`, helper `verify`, `verify-local` and `source-matches` exit 0
  - `sweep-partials --dry-run` lists nothing
  - restore after removing the source and local branch reproduces HEAD with a clean status
  - `verify-local` exits 1 after the remote branch is deleted
- `test-worktree-maintenance.py` (1 failure, 2 errors) and `test-worktree-recovery-lifecycle.sh` fail the same way on a clean `main` copy in this sandbox (managed-lifetime fixtures report not-enrolled).
- Not run on macOS. #36613 covers the macOS suite problems.
- `shellcheck` and `ruff` are clean on the changed files.

Resolves #36607

title: GH#36603: add dispatch pre-stage margin so admitted candidates clear the stage floor
body:
## Summary

Candidate admission (_dispatch_graphql_budget_allows_next) and the stage-start guard (_dispatch_cycle_budget_defers_candidate, GH#34428) both compared the cycle budget against the same 600s per-candidate floor, and every pre-dispatch reserve was sized to land dispatch exactly on that floor. When a clamped housekeeping stage used its full allowance, the pass arrived at admission a few seconds above 600s, pre-stage checks consumed those seconds, and every candidate deferred at 592-599s while slots stood idle. New _dispatch_prestage_margin_seconds (default 60s, DISPATCH_PRESTAGE_MARGIN_SECONDS, integer-validated, 0 restores old sizing) is added to candidate admission, to _dispatch_cycle_budget_admits_round (before and after enumeration, and round setup), and to every reserve that clamps stages ahead of dispatch: _pulse_dispatch_reserved_finalise_seconds and _pulse_first_wave_dispatch_reserve_seconds (via new _pulse_dispatch_admission_seconds), _preflight_post_label_refill_required_seconds, and the event-refill budget in _pulse_event_refill_apply_budget so its admission window stays PULSE_EVENT_REFILL_MAX_SECONDS. The stage-start guard keeps the bare floor, so no stage ever starts below 600s. Gate A's log line now reads 'below candidate admission reserve', so the issue's verification grep for 'below per-candidate floor' counts only stage-start deferrals.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-preflight-lib.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-event-refill.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh

## Decisions

Hysteresis by raising admission, not lowering the floor (the issue's 'floor = expected stage time' and 'always start first candidate' options would reintroduce rc=124 ceremony timeouts, t3043/GH#34428). Margin is 0 when the dispatch library defining it is not loaded, matching the admission gate defined alongside it. tests/test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh was already failing on main (PULSE_DIR unbound in the GH#36026 _pulse_rearm_blocker_holds preflight stage the fixture did not stub; unstubbed it would also invoke the live rearm helper); the fixture now stubs that stage so the first-wave reserve assertions run again. tests/test-pulse-wrapper-worker-detection.sh 'empty-snapshot login' fails identically before and after this change (login_calls=2) and is tracked separately.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** High
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — shellcheck -x clean on all 7 changed files. Baseline on the unmodified base: 10/12 suites pass; first-wave rc=1 (PULSE_DIR unbound) and worker-detection 1/40 FAIL (login_calls=2). After change: test-dispatch-max-parallel, test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring, test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave, test-pulse-event-refill, test-pulse-graphql-budget-priority, test-pulse-stale-blocked-reconcile, test-permission-block-breaker, test-pulse-dispatch-idle-debt-borrowing, test-pulse-dispatch-candidate-snapshot, test-pulse-dispatch-engine-timeout-floor, test-pulse-dispatch-stage-rc-adapter, test-terminal-blocker-circuit all rc=0; worker-detection unchanged (same single pre-existing FAIL). Pinned boundaries moved by the margin (959/960, 1060, 659/660); new assertions: margin=0 rollback admits at bare floor, invalid margin falls back to 60, and 630s remaining is refused by admission while the stage guard would proceed, 660s admitted. Runtime probe sourcing the real pulse-wrapper.sh with the real pulse-watchdog cycle clock (sandboxed HOME, only the GraphQL quota probe stubbed): default margin=60, reserved_finalise=first_wave=post_label=1050s (990s with DISPATCH_PRESTAGE_MARGIN_SECONDS=0); remaining~595 admission refuses + stage guard defers; ~630 admission refuses, guard would proceed; ~665 both proceed. Production check after deploy: per-cycle delta of 'below per-candidate floor' in pulse.log near zero over 6+ cycles, implementation_dispatched > 0 when active_workers < target.

Resolves #36603

title: GH#36622: fix(checkpoints): portable jq chunking so hidden-unedited normalisation works on jq 1.8
body:
## Summary

`_pcc_normalise_hidden_unedited` (added for #36529) chunked GraphQL node IDs with `_nwise(50)`. That is an undocumented jq internal, and jq 1.8 removed it. On jq 1.8 the jq call failed, `ids` fell back to empty, and the strict `updated_at` fence stayed in force. Comments that were hidden but never edited still read as edited, and `approval-template` kept refusing released checkpoints. Nothing errored visibly because the fallback fails closed.

This PR replaces `_nwise` with `. as $a | range(0; length; 50) | $a[.:.+50]`.

## Verification

- 120 IDs chunk to 50/50/20 on both jq 1.8.2 (macOS) and jq 1.7 (Linux runner). Empty input yields no chunks, so comments pass through unchanged.
- Real check on jq 1.8.2: `approval-template` for a draft whose previous continuation claim was hidden by dispatch hygiene (`lastEditedAt=null`, `isMinimized=true`) was refused with `reason=edited` before this change and emits the approval line after it.

title: GH#36620: fix(worker-lifecycle): raise journal event cap to 100,000 and lift legacy 10,000 stores
body:
## Summary

New lifecycle stores default to a 100,000-event journal (DEFAULT_MAX_EVENTS) instead of 10,000. Existing stores still at the legacy 10,000 default are lifted to 100,000 inside their next event write (_event -> _event_limit(lift=True)), in the same BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction as the event, so the lift commits or rolls back with it. Explicitly configured limits other than 10,000 are kept. status/summary reports the effective limit without writing. 100,000 is already the schema CHECK maximum, so no migration is needed. REGISTRY.md documents the new default and lift. Ordinary work filled 10,000 events in 6.1 days on a maintainer host (peak ~3,500/day), which blocked bounded operations, worktree creation and an authorized release. Retention remains #36618.

## Decisions

Lift only the exact legacy default (10,000) so deliberate small limits (tests use 1-3) keep their contract. Lift lazily inside the write transaction instead of a separate migration command, so every installation self-heals on its next event with no setup step and no partial state.
