title: t18860: GH#36628 fix(screen-time): measure Linux screen time from sampled human input activity
body:
## Summary

The profile README row "Screen time (Linux)" now measures sampled human input activity. Before this change it measured login-session or lock/lid state, which shows about 24h/day on always-on hosts and on SSH/tmux sessions. The macOS row is unchanged: it still uses display-backlit / app-usage intervals.

Resolves #36628

## What changed

- `.agents/scripts/screen_time_linux.py`: rewritten probe. Each sample reads only input timestamps, never keystrokes, window titles or content:
  - terminal sessions (SSH, console, attached tmux/screen clients): the access time of `/dev/<tty>`, which the kernel advances only when the tty delivers input (the same signal `w` uses for IDLE);
  - graphical sessions: desktop idle time from GNOME Mutter IdleMonitor, `org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver` or `xprintidle`, else the logind `IdleHint`; a desktop that keeps no idle hint is reported as unobservable (`partial`), not as active;
  - locked sessions and closing sessions are never counted.
- `.agents/scripts/screen_time_linux_activity.py` (new): a locked, atomic state machine that turns samples into compact `active` and `coverage` intervals in `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/observability/screen-activity.jsonl`. An active interval ends 300s after the last input (`AIDEVOPS_SCREEN_ACTIVITY_IDLE_SECONDS`) and never crosses a suspend, shutdown or sampler gap. Records are kept for a year and pruned once per local day.
- Removed `screen_time_linux_logind.py` and `screen_time_linux_wtmp.py`, the login-session proxies.
- `.agents/scripts/screen-time-interval-engine.py`, `screen_time_history.py`, `screen-time-helper.sh`: new `sample`, `collector` and `history-dates` commands. Snapshot rows are tagged with their collector, and Linux history ignores older rows that lack the `linux-input-activity` collector, so the old ~24h/day rows no longer inflate week/month/year totals. Linux reports `unavailable` until the sampler has data.
- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers.sh`: on Linux, installs the per-minute `aidevops-screen-activity-sampler` (systemd user timer, falling back to cron) next to the existing 6-hourly snapshot. It runs on update anywhere the snapshot scheduler is already installed.
- `.agents/scripts/routines/core-routines.sh`: the r909 Linux "what to check" line now points to the activity data.
- Tests: the old Linux proxy tests in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-screen-time-helper.sh` are replaced by activity-interval and probe-fixture tests, and the module copy lists are updated in both screen-time test suites.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-screen-time-helper.sh`: 14/14 PASS. It also passes with `AIDEVOPS_SCREEN_ACTIVITY_IDLE_SECONDS=600`, which confirms the suite is isolated from the caller's environment.
- `shellcheck` on every touched shell file: clean. `python3 -m py_compile` on the touched Python modules: clean. `radon cc`: no new function above B.
- Probe of the interval engine: 60 min of input, then 58 min idle, then a 2h sampler gap, then input. Result: three intervals, 1.2h total. The idle tail and the gap are excluded.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-profile-readme-boundary.sh` on macOS: all screen/rendering cases pass. 11 publication-worktree cases fail with `state-parent-must-be-canonical`, but `origin/main` fails the same 11 cases on this host (`/var/folders` is a symlinked tmp root), so this PR does not cause them.

## Notes

- Existing Linux users get real numbers only after the sampler has collected data, so the first completed day appears the day after they update. Until then the row shows `unavailable` instead of an inflated figure.
- Not checked on a real Linux desktop in this session (the dev host is macOS). Fixtures cover the logind/tty/desktop-idle parsing.

title: fix: retain lifecycle journal headroom with archive-first compaction (GH#36636)
body:
## Summary

Resolves #36636.

- Add archive-first lifecycle event retention while preserving run, binding and generation projections.
- Add dry-run/apply `compact` and backed-up `raise-capacity` recovery commands.
- Report three-event admission headroom and actionable OpenCode capacity refusals.

## Implementation context

Files: `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/storage.py`, `registry.py`, and `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/lifecycle-admission.mjs`; acceptance coverage is in `tests/test_events.py` and `tests/test_admission.py`.
Pattern: existing SQLite writer transactions and private archive-before-delete lifecycle operations.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — final head `1c53e36de7483f1a04871e92344aa3c3f709d5ff`; 57 event/admission/storage/upgrade tests and three bounded-worktree ownership integration tests pass. JavaScript syntax and `git diff --check` pass.

Commands:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=.agents/worker-lifecycle:.agents/worker-lifecycle/tests python3 -B -m unittest test_events test_admission test_storage test_upgrade -q
node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-bounded-worktree-ownership.mjs
node --check .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/lifecycle-admission.mjs
```

The retention regression fills a five-event store, ages the ended owner evidence, admits a new owner through the real transactional admission path, and verifies ended-owner replay conflicts. CLI tests verify default preview, explicit apply, archive checksums and recoverable IDs, backup integrity, age restrictions, and insufficient three-event headroom. Shared bound-owner evidence stays online. A real OpenCode bounded-operation start also succeeded on this runner; this does not claim a production at-capacity store was modified or deployed.

Full existing suite executed: 265 tests, 8 failures and 50 errors. Failures are outside this change: writable fixture configs are rejected with `unsafe-repository-config` under inherited `umask 0002`; a filesystem test assumes no sealed temporary ancestor, unlike this sandbox. Five representative failing tests reproduced unchanged on an exported `origin/main` (`234dd7041`):

- `test_absence.AbsenceContract.test_access_failure_is_not_absence_or_archive_failure`
- `test_filesystem.FilesystemContract.test_group_write_requires_private_group_or_sealed_ancestor`
- `test_launcher_paths.LauncherPathsContract.test_cleanup_entrypoints_use_registry_without_legacy_fallback`
- `test_legacy_cleanup.LegacyCleanupContract.test_pulse_runs_backlog_pass_without_admissions`
- `test_retirement.RetirementContract.test_enrolled_only_invalid_archive_keeps_admission_open`

No cleanup policy or filesystem validation was weakened to hide those baseline failures. Ruff/Mypy are unavailable locally; `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml` runs the pinned lifecycle lint, Linux/Darwin typechecks, and full lifecycle suite. Push-hook TypeScript verification could not start because `tsc` is absent and explicitly deferred to CI; no hooks were skipped.

## Review

Independent storage safety review found no remaining blocking defects. Addressed its concrete findings with durable event-ID/payload-digest tombstones and effective legacy-limit validation. Full journals containing only live/ineligible state still fail closed; capacity raising never exceeds the existing schema cap or truncates state.

Final closeout bundle: `9435970cb1fad7798c51ed20900620d799391a60da2d5f9796518292a631a263` (prompt-injection scan clean). Final type annotation does not change reviewed runtime behavior.

## Decisions

Preserve GH#36620's existing legacy capacity lift. Automatic retention defaults to one day, configurable with `AIDEVOPS_LIFECYCLE_RETENTION_SECONDS`. Each bounded archive batch is an immutable new file with canonical JSON evidence and SHA-256 checksum; rolled-back transactions retain evidence rather than overwrite it.

Recovery: `worker-registry.py --state-dir <state-directory> compact` previews at most 1000 eligible events; repeat with `--apply` to archive and delete that batch. `--min-age-seconds` explicitly overrides the age. Repeat batches as needed. `raise-capacity --max-events <higher-limit>` also previews by default; `--apply` first writes and verifies a standalone private SQLite backup. All run, generation and binding projections remain intact.

title: GH#36646: fix(GH#36646): record terminal-lease outbox row at ready transition so killed checkpoint workers are drained
body:
## Summary

Checkpoint workers now write the local terminal_lease_pending row right after their ready transition, from the worker process itself (same pid as the exit path), so the row carries a real process identity. A worker killed before its exit hook is then drained by the existing pulse recovery (expiry grace, executor_live, closed-issue skip, limit 3, close-expired-pr-checkpoint-lease as the only GitHub writer). A successful terminal post appends terminal_lease_resolved (append() previously dropped it because no pending row existed); a failed exit reuses the deduplicated row. Recording at claim time was not used: the claim runs in the dispatcher before the worker exists, so no worker identity could be captured and the row would be blocked as identity_unavailable.



## Files Changed

title: GH#36653: fix(consolidation): require exact consolidated-spec marker in successor validator
body:
## Summary

Consolidated successor issues filed without the exact `_Supersedes #N — this issue is the consolidated spec._` line, or with extra text on that line, are refused by the GH#23187 `_has_consolidated_label` gate on every pulse cycle. This change makes the pre-publication validator catch that before the successor is filed.

- `.agents/scripts/consolidation-contract-validator.py`: `validate()` now requires at least one line that exactly matches the marker regex shared with `pulse-dispatch-commit-gates.sh:494`, `dispatch-dedup-pr.sh:267` and `pulse-issue-reconcile-actions.sh:1294`. Lines split on LF only and body files are read without newline translation. The jq gate does not strip CR, so CRLF or trailing whitespace on the marker line is rejected too. When a near-miss `_Supersedes` line exists, the error says to put extra lineage on a separate line. The CLI now requires one unique `--parent N` per `--source`. Each parent needs its own marker line, and a marker number that is not a parent is rejected. The gate contract itself is unchanged.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-triage-dispatch.sh`: the consolidation-task instructions now say the marker is a line by itself, that extra lineage goes on a separate line, and that each additional superseded issue gets its own marker line. The validator command now passes `--parent ${parent_num}`. Step 4 now closes and repoints every superseded parent, not only the first.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-consolidation-contract-validator.py`: the existing fixtures now carry the marker. New cases cover a missing marker, prose-only "supersedes", trailing text, trailing whitespace, CRLF, an ASCII hyphen, lineage on a separate line, `--parent` matching, missing, extra and duplicate `--parent` arguments, and the CLI error naming the expected line. The new CLI cases run in-process to avoid new Bandit B603 findings.

CodeRabbit's three findings are addressed: CRLF bytes are preserved for the marker check, `--parent` must match `--source` one-to-one, and parent closure covers every parent. The optional attention-record follow-up from the issue is not included.

title: fix: fence runtime releases to owned dispatch claims (GH#36593)
body:
## Summary

Prevent runtime cleanup from posting an unmatched `CLAIM_RELEASED` or projecting lifecycle state for a dispatch generation it does not own.

Ref #36593. This is the separate producer-prevention change, not historical checkpoint reconciliation. The recovery report remains open, and its `no-auto-dispatch` and `hold-for-review` restrictions remain unchanged.

## Implementation

- Add `headless-runtime-release-claim.sh` and `dispatch-release-claim.jq` to match an actual claim using the authenticated author, runner, nonce/lease token, device and session.
- Reject ambiguous or edited evidence; treat absent, replaced, terminal or already-released claims as conservative no-ops.
- Require positive GraphQL `lastEditedAt: null` evidence for comments authorizing a write, even when REST timestamps match. Equal second-resolution REST timestamps cannot exclude a same-second edit. Minimized but unedited comments remain supported.
- Recheck the original claim generation before posting, on persistence retries, after posting and before normal lifecycle projection. Bind new release records to the exact claim ID and dispatch identity.
- Preserve issue lifecycle state when post-write ownership is superseded or unavailable, and direct operators to reconcile persisted comments rather than blindly replay.
- Extend existing focused fixtures for absent/mismatched claims, duplicate or malformed evidence, pagination, replacement-claim races, same-second edits, incomplete GraphQL metadata and edited post-release evidence.
- Integrate current upstream terminal-lease recovery, isolate its fixture outbox, and extract cohesive helpers to satisfy the existing function-length gate without an override.

## Runtime Testing

Executed locally against the integrated `origin/main` base:

```text
bash .agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed --base-ref origin/main
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-release-unlock.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-rate-limit-release-circuit.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-atomic-lease.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh
python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-claim-only.py
python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-revision.py
```

All passed. Terminal-blocker suite: 56 tests, zero failures. Checkpoint claim-only suite: 39 tests passed; revision suite: 24 passed. The changed-file linter passed its required ShellCheck, secret, portability, compatibility and complexity checks; historical shell-formatting differences remain advisory. The pre-push repository typecheck and quality hooks also passed.

These are isolated fixture-based checks of the existing CLI/runtime release path, not evidence of hosted execution, deployment or historical recovery. Independent local read-only review identified the same-second edit gap in the first commit; the follow-up repaired it, added focused coverage, and was re-reviewed without another concrete unsafe-write finding.

## Risk and boundaries

Risk: high, because this path controls coordination writes and lifecycle projection. Missing or ambiguous ownership/edit evidence retains state rather than granting permission to release.

- The guard is a snapshot fence, not an atomic GitHub compare-and-swap. A residual check/write race remains; generation-bound records and fresh post-write checks reduce stale projection but do not eliminate that race.
- The existing lease reader already recognizes an authenticated exact claim-ID/nonce release as terminal. The updated atomic-lease fixture verifies that behavior while retaining rejection coverage for unbound releases.
- GraphQL edit evidence adds bounded, batched reads and becomes necessary for writes; API outages or incomplete metadata can defer cleanup.
- Historical checkpoint readers and revision-approval policy are unchanged. No published coordination events are edited, deleted or reconstructed, and existing unsupported histories remain blocked.
- No downstream checkpoint continuation, publication replay, authentication, catalogue write, installation, release or deployment is performed or authorized by this PR.

## Review focus

Review the ownership and edit fences in `headless-runtime-release-claim.sh` / `dispatch-release-claim.jq`, their integration in `headless-runtime-failure.sh`, and the focused existing tests above. In particular, verify that missing receipts or post-write uncertainty never authorize a replay or a lifecycle mutation.

title: GH#36704: fix(pulse): stop one Dependabot replacement PR from stalling the Dependabot queue
body:
## Summary

Root cause: replacement PR #36590 (Resolves #36583) also says 'Then close #36582 as superseded'; #36582 is the Dependabot source PR. _extract_linked_issue counted both numbers, logged 'ambiguous closing issue identities' every cycle, and the merge pass returned without a decision for 28h. #36583 stayed in review, and because every Dependabot intake listed .agents/configs/trusted-dependabot-updates.conf in its Files Scope, all other intakes (npm and GitHub Actions) were footprint-deferred behind it. GH#36683 fixed the same false link in maintainer-gate-reusable.yml only. Fix: (1) _extract_linked_issue drops closing targets that the issues API reports as pull requests, only when several candidates exist, so the single-target path makes no new API calls; lookup failures keep the number (fail closed). (2) approval-required intakes no longer declare the shared allowlist, which their brief forbids editing, so independent updates stop serializing on it. (3) The intake brief tells workers to reference the source as 'Supersedes #N' and leaves source closure to pulse, which already closes it after the replacement merges (GH#30478). Approval and trust gates are unchanged.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/pulse-dependabot-intake.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dependabot-intake.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-extract-linked-issue.sh

## Decisions

Filter PR refs only when a body is ambiguous: this fixes the observed failure without adding a per-cycle API call to every PR that has one closing keyword. Allowlist scope stays for policy-ineligible intakes, where an allowlist edit is a valid resolution. No change to crypto-approval or Dependabot trust checks.

title: GH#36707: fix(pulse): plan capacity for selector fallback when preferred provider pool is exhausted
body:
## Summary

Resolves #36707

Pulse planned dispatch capacity against the preferred provider even when that provider's OAuth pool had no usable accounts. Two causes combined:

1. **Inherited pool token treated as static capacity.** The OpenCode plugin exports the selected Anthropic pool token as `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. Child processes (pulse, headless selection) inherited it, so `provider_static_auth_available anthropic` reported independent static-key capacity and bypassed the pool cooldown gate. OpenAI already had an `AIDEVOPS_OPENAI_API_KEY_SOURCE=oauth-pool` marker; Anthropic did not.
2. **Capacity never consulted the worker selector.** `pulse_apply_provider_load_capacity_cap` derived the planning provider from credential presence, so an exhausted preferred pool zeroed global capacity even when the worker selector would launch a healthy fallback provider.

## Changes

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/{oauth-pool,provider-auth,provider-auth-pool-recovery,v2-provider-auth}.mjs`: set `AIDEVOPS_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY_SOURCE=oauth-pool` at every site that writes the pool token into `process.env`.
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-provider.sh`: `provider_static_auth_available anthropic` ignores pool-derived env tokens (mirrors the OpenAI rule).
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-capacity.sh`: new `_pulse_capacity_fallback_provider` asks `headless-runtime-helper.sh select --role worker --tier standard` (about 0.4s, bounded by `timeout_sec 20`) when the planning provider has zero available accounts. Capacity is then planned for that provider's pool and a `provider_fallback` line is logged. Explicit `PULSE_DISPATCH_CAPACITY_PROVIDER` stays authoritative. Provider and count resolution moved into `_pulse_capacity_resolve_provider_accounts` to keep the cap function under the 100-line complexity limit.

## Verification

- `shellcheck` on changed shell files; `node --check` on the 4 plugin files.
- `test-dispatch-min-concurrency.sh` 32/32, including a new case: Anthropic pool exhausted + selector picks OpenAI → `24 0 24`; with an explicit `PULSE_DISPATCH_CAPACITY_PROVIDER=anthropic` pin → `0 0 0`.
- `test-headless-runtime-oauth-pool-gate.sh`: new cases where an inherited pool-derived Anthropic key falls back to OpenAI and an independent Anthropic key still bypasses the cooldown gate.
- Also passed: `test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh` (73/73), `test-pulse-current-state-guardrails.sh` (27/27), `test-pulse-ram-admission.sh`, `test-maintenance-selector-contract.sh`, `test-headless-provider-round-robin.sh`, `test-headless-routing-retry.sh`, `test-headless-runtime-contract-tests.sh`.

body:
## Summary
- Capture one explicit `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_QUESTION` only from the final assistant report for an input-required blocker; clear it between attempts.
- Publish `Input requested:` only for a bounded question that passes credential scrubbing, private-entity/path guards and additional public-text validation. Never copy the raw BLOCKED dossier.
- When missing or unsafe, explicitly tell the originating recovery supervisor to publish a sanitized question instead of implying that the maintainer can read private telemetry.
- Extend the worker completion contract and existing circuit/lifecycle regression suites.

Resolves #36760

## Files and reference pattern
- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`: existing final-report capture and recovery observation renderer; reuse shared credential/privacy helpers.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-prompt.sh`: shared first-pass contract used by normal, clean-room and fallback launches.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` and `test-dispatch-lifecycle-comms.sh`: extend existing harnesses, no new infrastructure.

## Runtime Testing
Risk: medium; testing: runtime-verified on Bash 5.3.9 / Python 3.13.17. Exact tested head: `7e3c588ed768bdb84c48f70ecc6940e253ebb2f3`.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`: 57 tests, 0 failures.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-lifecycle-comms.sh`: 27 tests, 0 failures.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-terminal-blockers.sh`: 13 tests, 0 failures.
- `bash -n` on all four changed shell files and `git diff --check`: pass.
- Pre-commit and pre-push hooks: pass after making synthetic sensitive-shaped fixtures public-safe.
- Independent bounded review: no concrete privacy/cross-attempt findings.

## Tooling limitations
The installed ShellCheck wrapper cannot locate a real binary, and no worktree-local `.venv/bin/shellcheck` is available. ShellCheck is covered by `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml`, job `cross-platform-shellcheck` (ShellCheck ubuntu-latest). Root TypeScript checking could not start because tsc/dev dependencies are absent; the repository pre-push verifier explicitly defers it to `.github/workflows/typecheck.yml`. No JavaScript/TypeScript files or dependencies changed. These are CI handoffs, not claimed local passes.

## Decisions
Use an explicit public-safe question marker rather than infer from raw private prose. Reject unsafe/malformed questions and preserve blocker ownership, fingerprints, retry rules and permission/security guarantees. The optional pulse-cycle recovery policy is not changed.

title: GH#36593: fix(checkpoint): accept maintainer-acknowledged orphan releases as unattributed history (GH#36593)
body:
## Summary

Releases that follow fully closed checkpoint episodes with no claim of their own ("orphans") blocked every new revision-bound approval with `transition_rejected`. History now records each orphan as a `released_successors` entry with outcome `unattributed_release` and provenance `unrecovered`. `approval-template` refuses until the maintainer names the exact comment IDs with `--acknowledge-unattributed`, and `dispatch-approved` accepts only an approval that lists them exactly. These cases still reject: orphans inside open episodes, and edited, untrusted or malformed releases. Tokens that an orphan names stay fenced, and automatic approval paths never acknowledge orphans. Writer-side prevention already landed in dc2f620a33.

`worker-discipline.md` now classifies a fail-closed audit gap that can be safely recovered as an implementation task, not a review hold. Pulse and workers should have implemented this fix instead of holding it.

## Files Changed

- `.agents/scripts/pr_checkpoint_unattributed.py` (new; orphan-release representation, split out to keep file complexity down)
- `.agents/scripts/pr_checkpoint_history.py`, `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-revision.py`, `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-unattributed.py` (new), `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` (runs it)
- `.agents/reference/checkpoint-revision-recovery.md`, `.agents/reference/worker-discipline.md`

## Decisions

Maintainer decision recorded on #36593: implement this as an explicit, append-only acknowledgement rather than relaxing the validator. Acknowledgement is per comment ID and is carried in the signed approval, so it is auditable and bound to the head, brief revision and expiry.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** High
- **Verification:** runtime-verified.
  - `test-pr-checkpoint-unattributed.py` 3/3: exact acknowledgement, retained rejections, token fencing.

title: fix: share verified-unedited proof with checkpoint claims
body:
## Summary

Share verified-unedited comment normalization between checkpoint discovery, approval templates, and revision claim admission. Follow-up to the hidden-comment compatibility handling in #36529.

GitHub comment hygiene can change REST `updated_at` without editing a comment body. Template generation already checks GraphQL `lastEditedAt`, but the claim subprocess rereads raw REST comments and previously rejected the same preserved history as edited. An exact approval could therefore pass discovery and fail before posting a claim.

## Changes

- Move the existing normalizer from `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` into `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-target-lib.sh`.
- Apply the shared normalizer at `_pr_checkpoint_revised_target`, covering the claim producer's fresh snapshots before and after consensus as well as revision target verification.
- Require an explicit `lastEditedAt: null`; missing fields, unavailable metadata, missing nodes, and actual edits retain the strict edit fence.
- Preserve flat and paginated comment snapshot shapes and portable 50-node query chunking.
- Extend the existing continuation and revision suites with a minimized historical claim passing through the actual claim subprocess, flat snapshots, and missing-edit-field rejection. No new runner, fixture infrastructure, or CI gate.

## Safety boundaries

Revision/head/brief binding, permission checks, protective labels, ownership fences, claim consensus, lease transitions, and replay prevention remain enforced. This change does not infer successful work from historical releases.

No live continuation, hosted authentication, publication, data mutation, installation, release, or deployment was performed for this patch. This PR does not authorize those operations.

## Verification

- Before the production change, the added minimized-history integration case failed in the real claim subprocess after successful discovery.
- `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-revision.py`: **31 tests passed** after the fix.
- The continuation suite's companion Python suites passed: claim-only (39), private-member trust (5), self-hold (4), and unattributed history (3).
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`: **157 checks passed, 5 failed**. The shared-normalizer check and revised claim integration passed.
- `shellcheck` and `bash -n` passed for the changed shell files; `git diff --check` passed.
- `bash .agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed --base-ref HEAD^`: passed, including Secretlint, ShellCheck, portability, Python 3.9 annotations, jq compatibility, and regression ratchets. Existing shfmt and repeated-literal advisories remain unchanged.
- Pre-commit and pre-push hooks passed, including the pre-push typecheck.

### Existing continuation-suite failures

All five failures below also reproduced on untouched base `a25d22acb8a6be6d35002a0458306c5243d52b56` in a separate baseline worktree:

1. Released attempt's own terminal lease does not suppress blocked attention.
2. Terminal lease from `worker-bot/unseen-lease` still counts as ownership.
3. Terminal lease from `other-runner/closing-lease` still counts as ownership.
4. Never-ready blocked release names the checkpoint's own release and attempt.
5. Unpaired never-ready blocked release posts no approval template.

The baseline run was time-bounded and reproduced these five failures before its timeout; it is not evidence of a complete baseline suite pass. These attention/template assertions are outside this normalization fix. The full continuation suite is **not green**.

## Review focus

Check `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-target-lib.sh` for fail-closed GraphQL proof and fresh revision admission, and `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` for removal of the duplicate implementation. Regression coverage is in the two existing `test-pr-checkpoint-*` files changed by this PR.

title: GH#36698: fail over to the next same-tier model on OpenAI entitlement rejection
body:
## Summary

When OpenAI rejects a model for the current subscription (model_not_found, or the Codex not-supported-with-ChatGPT-account error), routing moves straight to the next connected candidate in the same tier and recovers automatically once access returns. Interactive (OpenCode plugin): the provider fetch guard records the definite rejection for the current OpenAI auth and returns the response unchanged (hardcoded slug swap removed; recordCodexModelRejection); the failed child Task is re-prompted on the next connected same-tier candidate in routing-table order, at most once per candidate, never a lower tier, never after side effects, with aidevopsRoutingFailover metadata; initial routing skips models rejected for the current auth and, when all same-tier candidates are rejected, the error names tier, requested model and rejected models; records are keyed by an opaque hash of the current OpenAI access token read at every routing decision, so a re-login clears them at once, else they expire after 15 minutes (max 256 entries). Headless: the classifier maps structured and plaintext entitlement rejections to model_unavailable (403 stays access_denied); model_unavailable records a model-keyed 1h backoff (other provider models stay usable; cleared on auth change), triggers exact-tier reselection inside the run, is soft at the dispatcher canary, is an infrastructure retry class, and is never a worker-side canary bypass. Docs: .agents/tools/context/model-routing.md Entitlement failover (GH#36698). Builds on contributor PR #36699 by @mikemikimike (head b2f98b97 merged into this branch, history preserved) and completes the six maintainer review items on that PR; branch is on current main a25d22acb8 (0 behind), and --no-rebase keeps the contributor merge commit.

title: fix(full-loop): verify registry retirement for cleanup receipts
body:
## Summary

Fix full-loop completion after native registry retirement has already preserved and removed a worktree, but no legacy `worktree-removed` text log exists. Previously `complete-after-cleanup` rejected that valid terminal state even when the archive and native retirement event were verifiable.

- Add read-only `verify-retirement` to the lifecycle registry CLI. It binds the cleanup receipt's repository, branch, source path and creation time to exactly one enrolled generation, terminal retirement event, preservation receipt and verified archive manifest.
- Let cleanup-receipt finalization accept this identity-bound proof when the legacy removal log is absent. Keep existing audited-removal compatibility.
- Remove the earlier legacy-log-only precondition from `complete-after-cleanup`; the exact durable cleanup-receipt verifier remains mandatory.
- Fail closed for replacement paths (including dangling symlinks), remaining admissions, mismatched identities, out-of-order receipt timestamps, ambiguous generations and changed archive manifests.

The reference pattern is the existing native retirement journal and preservation verifier, not a new cleanup authority. Verification does not remove a worktree, fabricate historical logs or admissions, mutate registry records, or authorize another retirement. No new runtime dependency, installation update or framework release is included.

- All 10 `test_retirement.py` enrolled-only cases passed, including the real archive-to-cleanup-receipt bridge and negative identity/archive checks.

title: fix: raise claude-cli UA fallback to 2.1.280 so claude-opus-5-5 is usable without the Claude CLI
body:
## Problem

Anthropic gates newer models on the Claude Code client version advertised in the
request `user-agent`. Selecting `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` in OpenCode fails for
any host that does not have the `claude` CLI on `PATH`:

```
level=ERROR message="stream error" providerID=anthropic modelID=claude-opus-5-5
error.error="AI_APICallError: Claude Code 2.1.80 does not support this model;
version 2.1.280 or newer is required. Run 'claude update', or update the
Claude desktop app, then try again."
```

Observed five times across three sessions and two projects on 2026-11-05 in
`~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`. The same account has zero stream
errors for `anthropic/claude-opus-5` (38 requests), so the failure is the client
version gate, not credentials or the model catalog.

## Cause

Anthropic OAuth requests have their `user-agent` rewritten to the Claude CLI
identity:

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/provider-auth-request.mjs:72` sets
  `user-agent` from `getAnthropicUserAgent()`.
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/oauth-pool-token-endpoint.mjs:80` builds it
  as `claude-cli/${DETECTED_CLAUDE_VERSION} (external, cli)`.
- `DETECTED_CLAUDE_VERSION` comes from `claude --version`; when the binary is
  absent the hardcoded fallback is used.

The fallback was pinned at `2.1.80`, which the API now rejects for
`claude-opus-5-5`, so every host without the Claude CLI loses access to the
model with a misleading "update Claude Code" message.

## Change

Raise the fallback to the lowest version that satisfies the current gate, in both
places that carry it:

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/oauth-pool-token-endpoint.mjs:29`
  (`FALLBACK_CLAUDE_VERSION`)
- `.agents/scripts/oauth-pool-helper.sh:99` (`CLAUDE_VERSION`)

Both gain a comment stating the invariant: the constant must stay at or above the
highest model gate the API enforces, so the next occurrence is diagnosable
without re-deriving it from logs.

Live detection is unchanged and still wins when `claude` is installed.
`.agents/scripts/cch-sign.py:331` is untouched: it derives the version from an
actual installed Claude Code bundle rather than a fallback.

## Verification

- `node --check .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/oauth-pool-token-endpoint.mjs` — pass
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/oauth-pool-helper.sh` — pass, no warnings
- `bash -n .agents/scripts/oauth-pool-helper.sh` — pass
- `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed` — exit 0 (shfmt, ShellCheck,
  secretlint, string-literal, bash32-compat, complexity, nesting, portability)
- Pre-commit hook quality validation — passed
- `rg '2\.1\.80' .agents` — no remaining references; no test asserted the old
  constant

## Residual risk

The constant is a version floor and will go stale again when Anthropic raises a
gate for a future model. The durable fix is detection coverage: the shim PATH
(`~/.local/bin/opencode`) does not include common Claude Code install locations
such as `~/.claude/local/`, so an installed CLI outside the exported PATH still
falls through to the constant. Worth a follow-up to widen the detection paths.

<!-- aidevops:origin:interactive -->

title: fix(checkpoints): reconcile acknowledged terminal-without-release history
body:
## Summary

Add a manual-only, revision-bound acknowledgement for a historical checkpoint episode containing a matching claim, ready lease and terminal lease but no preceding `CLAIM_RELEASED`. Default and automatic continuation remain fail closed.

## Linked issue

Ref #36593. This is a distinct historical shape: that delivered fix acknowledges standalone releases after fully closed episodes; it does not reconcile a terminal lease inside an incompletely closed episode. This PR does not claim to fix, reopen or close that prior issue, and contains no downstream identifiers or private evidence.

## Changes and reference pattern

- `.agents/scripts/pr_checkpoint_history.py`: reconstruct only explicitly acknowledged terminal comment IDs with matching trusted, unedited actor/device/session/token/attempt evidence, known positive expiries elapsed at approval time, strict claim/ready/terminal order and `expires_at=0`. Emit `terminal_without_release`, `release_provenance: missing` and `execution_status: unrecovered`; never invent a release.
- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-revision.py`: bind the exact anomalous entry and an SHA-256 fingerprint of all its coordination records, including intermediate renewals, to the existing head/ref/brief-bound approval. Reconstruct at the approval timestamp and fence the historical token from reuse.
- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`: add `--acknowledge-terminal-without-release=ID[,ID]`, composable with the existing exact orphan-release acknowledgement. Unknown/repeated options fail closed. Automatic callers supply neither flag.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-unattributed.py`: extend the existing offline GitHub fixtures and suites; no new runner or CI gate.
- `.agents/reference/checkpoint-revision-recovery.md`: document the narrow recovery decision, required independent executor shutdown/fencing and current ownership checks, explicit uncertainty and unchanged continuation boundaries.

The reference pattern is the existing `unattributed_release` acknowledgement and exact `released_successors` validation, not an automatic takeover or fabricated normal lifecycle.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Documentation

## Runtime Testing

**Testing level:** `runtime-verified` for the CLI using the existing offline GitHub fixture only. No live GitHub recovery, downstream executor, application server, beta authentication or catalogue operation was exercised.

| Check | Result | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CLI acknowledgement and combined options | Pass | Real CLI entry point against existing offline GitHub transport; fixture state unchanged |
| Acknowledgement regression suite | Pass | 10 tests |
| Revision-bound approval suite | Pass | 31 tests |
| Claim-only and expired-ready suite | Pass | 39 tests |
| Changed-file quality gates | Pass | `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed --base-ref origin/main`; ShellCheck, secret scanning, Markdown and portability/complexity checks |
| Commit and push hooks | Pass | No bypass; push hook also ran `bun run typecheck` successfully |
| Full continuation shell suite | Fail, baseline reproduced | Five of 162 shell assertions fail identically on the unchanged baseline; see below |

The full shell suite also ran and passed its embedded private-member (5 tests) and self-hold (4 tests) Python suites. Reported SQLite ResourceWarnings in the revision suite did not fail that suite; no cleanup change is included here.

### Baseline failures, not a green full-suite claim

Command: `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`.

The same five shell assertions failed on both this candidate and unchanged baseline `cebac75a221fbd0c839f8ed3bf3416df584fb6b4`:

1. Released attempt's own terminal lease does not suppress blocked attention.
2. Terminal lease with an unseen lease still counts as ownership.
3. Terminal lease from another runner still counts as ownership.
4. Never-ready blocked release names the checkpoint's own release and attempt.
5. Unpaired never-ready blocked release posts no approval template.

Their cause is not established by this PR. No unrelated test expectations or attention behavior were modified. Do not treat these results as a fully green shell suite.

### Security review and authority limits

This changes orchestration authorization/history validation, so it needs security-sensitive review. Independent static review identified an initial intermediate-record binding gap; the final patch fingerprints all episode coordination records and tests deletion of intermediate evidence. The bounded recheck found no remaining concrete defects; it was not an independent runtime test or maintainer approval.

The flag acknowledges an audit gap, not proof that execution stopped or no external writes occurred. Maintainers must separately verify executor shutdown/fencing and current ownership before approving. Later interactive claims, open/overlapping owners, foreign/edited records, unknown/live expiries, changed head/brief and stale approvals remain rejecting cases. Fresh fenced claim acquisition remains mandatory. Original events are preserved and consumed operations must not be replayed.

This PR is intentionally draft for review. It authorizes no installation, release, downstream checkpoint takeover, authentication, deployment, data write or closure of a downstream objective. No installed framework files, application code or downstream checkpoint files are changed.

## Checklist

- [x] Includes a non-closing framework issue reference
- [x] Conventional commit message
- [x] Narrow recovery documentation updated
- [x] Operator authorized scoped implementation and commit/push/PR creation
- [ ] Maintainer security review and merge decision
- [ ] Required remote checks reviewed at the exact head

title: GH#36883: fix(worktree-archive): preserve runtime-local config.worktree bytes without restoring them
body:
## Summary

Git-only worktree archives refused every non-empty `config.worktree` (`git_admin:requires_preservation:config.worktree`), and no other creation policy is left (`--preserve-git-admin` / `preserve-v1` are rejected). So every Codex worktree whose `config.worktree` held `codex.localenvironmentconfigpath` was retained on every cleanup pass.

This PR implements the approved resolution plan from https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/36883#issuecomment-6687798094:

- **Classify** (`worktree_archive_runtime_config.py`, new): a file is accepted only if it parses, has at least one key, and every lower-cased key is in `RUNTIME_LOCAL_CONFIG_KEYS = {codex.localenvironmentconfigpath}`. Unknown keys, mixed keys and comment-only files keep the existing refusal. `core.worktree` and `include*.path` keep their earlier `location_dependent_config` refusal.
- **Capture** (`worktree_archive_index.py`, `worktree-archive-helper.sh`): accepted bytes are written exactly to the 0600 `worktree-config-v1` artifact inside the 0700 archive.
- **Fingerprint** (`worktree_archive_fingerprint.py`): optional `config_worktree_sha256` plus `config_worktree_keys` (names only, never values). `source-matches` therefore refuses retirement if the config appears, changes or disappears after capture.
- **Verify** (`verify_archive` inventory plus `verify()`): the artifact is mandatory when the fingerprint names it and forbidden otherwise. Its hash must match the fingerprint, and the classifier is re-run on the archived bytes, so an artifact with a non-runtime key fails even when the manifest is rewritten to match.
- **Restore**: never writes `config.worktree` and never changes `extensions.worktreeConfig`. `restore` prints the omitted key names on stderr. The canonical restore receipt records `omitted_runtime_config`. The restore-proof comparison excludes only the two runtime-config fingerprint fields (`restored_view`).
- **Docs**: `worktree-archive-helper.md` now states the actual contract in place of "Preserve that configuration separately".

Out of scope, unchanged: pending merges with `config.worktree` (still refused by `supported_merge_administration`), generic preservation of arbitrary keys, and `legacy_cleanup.py` (reaches capture through the existing path; failures still map to `retained`).

## Files Changed

- `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_runtime_config.py` (new)
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_index.py`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_fingerprint.py`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_restore.py`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree-archive-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree-archive-helper.md`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/worktree_archive_administration_cases.py`

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** High (archive format and retirement boundary). Unknown configuration stays fail-closed, and the bytes are always preserved.
- Existing runner `test-worktree-archive-lifecycle.py`: the refusal test now also covers mixed Codex plus unknown keys and a symlinked config. The new case `test_runtime_local_worktree_config_is_preserved_not_restored` covers capture, verify, `source-matches`, `restore` without `config.worktree` (key reported, value absent), the canonical restore proof with `omitted_runtime_config`, drift (changed, removed, added after capture) and tamper (rewritten artifact with a consistent manifest).
- Results: full lifecycle suite 183 OK (24 skipped); worker-lifecycle preservation 12 OK (1 skipped); ShellCheck clean. Details: https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/pull/36895#issuecomment-6689361200

Resolves #36883

body:
## Summary

- Add `aidevops tabby sessions host add|update|remove|list|show` for local host inventory management, including disabled hosts and dry runs.
- Register existing SSH aliases or create explicitly managed aliases in a separate OpenSSH Include file. Keep SSH changes out of user-owned alias blocks.
- Report the selected inventory and refuse temporary smoke-test targets by default, preventing accidental edits through a stale `AIDEVOPS_TABBY_HOSTS` override.

## Implementation and ownership

- `.agents/scripts/tabby_session_hosts.py` and `tabby_host_inventory.py`: host-command routing, arguments, inventory CRUD, and explicit SSH ownership/removal checks; reuse validation from `tabby_session_config.py`.
- `.agents/scripts/tabby_host_ssh.py` and `tabby_host_ssh_scan.py`: strict managed-file serialization and conservative conflict discovery through local OpenSSH Includes.
- `.agents/scripts/tabby_host_files.py`: private backups outside SSH Include globs, serialized cooperating writers, per-file atomic replacement, and partial-write rollback.
- `.agents/scripts/tabby_sessions.py` and `tabby-helper.sh`: route and advertise the new host subcommand without changing existing session actions.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-tabby-sessions.py`: extend the existing isolated acceptance suite rather than adding a runner.
- `.agents/tools/terminal/remote-sessions.md`: document examples, configuration precedence, migration boundaries, and recovery behavior.

## Safety and limitations

- Ordinary removal keeps the SSH alias. `remove --ssh` only removes an aidevops-managed alias without another reference in the selected inventory; references in other inventory files cannot be checked automatically.
- Refuse externally edited managed files, conflicting user-owned aliases, symlink paths, hardlinked/non-owned files, and group/world-writable configuration files.
- Conditional SSH `Match` rules require manual SSH configuration: refuse SSH edits rather than executing or guessing rules that might own the alias. `Host *` and `Match all` defaults remain supported. Existing-alias registration and inventory-only updates remain available.
- Busy configuration locks fail immediately with a retry message. Extra top-level inventory metadata is preserved, matching the existing session loader's compatibility contract.
- Multi-file updates are not crash-atomic. Write failures attempt rollback and explicitly report incomplete rollback; private backups are retained.
- No changes to SSH host-key verification, keys, known-host entries, running tmux sessions, tabs, or attachment leases. Existing local OpenSSH `Match exec` behavior still applies to registration's `ssh -G` check.

title: fix(worker): accept fractional cleanup receipt timestamps
body:
## Summary

- Accept fractional-second UTC `created_at` timestamps from guarded cleanup receipts in the worker's own-merged completion verifier.
- Normalize only the fractional suffix before jq's whole-second `fromdateiso8601` parser; retain the existing attempt-start freshness comparison and all ownership, exact-head, issue-linkage, clean-worktree and finalization checks.
- Extend the existing reconciliation cases to cover a valid fractional receipt, a stale fractional receipt and a malformed receipt timestamp.

## Problem and evidence

During worker-failure diagnosis, merged deliveries with finalized cleanup receipts were classified as premature exits with `pr_less_completion_rejected` / `unpublished_local_commits`. The own-merged verifier silently rejected the receipt first: Python-generated timestamps such as `2026-11-06T04:38:03.813577Z` fail jq's `fromdateiso8601`, which accepts the whole-second UTC form.

This change repairs the timestamp mismatch rather than weakening the fallback no-unpublished-work guard. Receipts that are stale, unfinalized, foreign-session, wrong-head or associated with unpublished edits remain rejected. Existing historical metrics are not rewritten.

## Files and reference pattern

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh`: `_hrw_own_merged_terminal_complete`, retaining its existing guarded receipt contract.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-provider-tests.sh`: extend `_setup_own_merged_evidence` and `test_own_merged_terminal_reconciliation` in the current test harness; no new infrastructure.

## Verification

title: GH#36913: auto-refresh profile README Projects; fix CONTRIBUTIONS marker collision
body:
## Summary

New public repositories never appeared on the GitHub profile README. Two root causes, both in `.agents/scripts/profile-readme-helper.sh`:

1. **Projects was a one-time snapshot.** `_generate_rich_readme` wrote `## Projects` once at `init`; the hourly `update` never touched it. The live profile was missing 6 public repos created since September 2026.
2. **Daily Contributions refresh failed silently.** `_contribution_marker_state` counted `CONTRIBUTIONS-START` via `grep -F`, which also matched `<!-- TOTAL-CONTRIBUTIONS-START -->`. Every profile with the total-contributions chart was classified `invalid` (`Contributions markers must be one standalone, ordered pair` on each daily run in `profile-readme-update.log`), so new forks/contributions never refreshed either.

## Changes

- `_generate_projects`: public, non-fork, non-archived repos owned by the user, excluding the profile repo; ordered by stars then name; descriptions sanitized (`[]()\`<>` stripped), URLs restricted to `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>`; private repos filtered as defence in depth. API failure or malformed response fails closed.
- `<!-- PROJECTS-START -->`/`<!-- PROJECTS-END -->` block refreshed on every `update` (`_refresh_projects_block`, applied to the candidate before the no-op comparison). Any failure preserves the previous block and never blocks stats publication.
- `_projects_ensure_markers`: adopts the static `## Projects` section only in aidevops-generated READMEs (`> Stats auto-updated by [aidevops]`); hand-written READMEs opt in by adding the markers. Malformed marker topology is preserved untouched.
- `init` emits the markers through the same generator.
- `_count_marker_mentions`: whole-token marker counting, so `TOTAL-CONTRIBUTIONS-*` no longer collides with `CONTRIBUTIONS-*`.
- Regression case in `test-profile-readme-contributions-fail-closed.sh` for the chart-block collision.

## Verification

- Live profile README, function-level dry-run: migration to markers, the 6 missing repos added, archived `aidevops-dashboard` excluded, second refresh byte-identical, a stubbed `gh` failure leaves the block unchanged.
- `_contribution_marker_state` on the live README: `invalid` on `main` → `valid` on this branch.
- `test-profile-readme-boundary.sh`: passes locally (exit 0).
- `test-profile-readme-contributions-fail-closed.sh`: locally, 17 cases fail on both `main` and this branch with the same host-specific `Native worktree creation refused ... FileNotFoundError`; CI (`code-quality.yml`) is the authoritative run.
- `shellcheck -x`, `/bin/bash -n`, and the pre-commit ratchets pass.

Resolves #36913

title: fix(pulse): resume housekeeping and verify delayed runtime starts
body:
## Summary

Fix housekeeping starvation and activation verification defects observed on a current Linux runner with 38 pulse-enabled repositories:

- Reconciliation's cooperative budget stayed at 360 seconds even when its watchdog allocation was around 160 seconds. Clamp it to the actual allocation minus the existing 20-second grace, while preserving shorter configured budgets.
- Dependency graph rebuilds persisted only after the final repository. Repeated stage timeouts discarded completed repository reads; the operational cache had not completed a rebuild since October 29. Checkpoint each repository atomically, retain original per-repository freshness, and resume oldest snapshots first.
- Unmanaged Linux starts checked for an activated runtime lease only once after the launch grace. Reuse the existing bounded verification loop, which already rejects stale/wrong-runtime processes. A delayed-lease regression fails before this change and passes afterward.
- Isolated v1 workers could attach to an ambient OpenCode server, bypassing their seeded database and provider-scoped authentication. Keep default isolated runs standalone; retain ambient attachment only for explicitly non-isolated v1 runs. Ephemeral roles and v2 stay standalone.
- Reviewer follow-up: incomplete graph checkpoints remain eligible for async catch-up regardless of fresh mtime. Budgeted reconciliation alternates repair-first and issue-first priority using a durable sidecar written before slow work, and preserves saved issue positions when repair work consumes the budget or is interrupted.

An incomplete checkpoint bypasses the ordinary cache TTL and a deadline yield returns 124 so blocker catch-up remains retryable. Disabled repositories are excluded. Existing ownership, API admission, dependency and stale-evidence safety checks remain intact; no concurrency, scheduler defaults or permissions are changed.

## Linked issue

Ref #33246

title: GH#36961: review-bot-gate evaluates fork PRs on pull_request_target so the required status is posted
body:
## Summary

The required review-bot-gate context is a commit status. Fork pull_request runs get Statuses: read and the post fails with 403. On fork PRs, the status was written only when a review bot commented (a base-context issue_comment run). A silent CodeRabbit left the status stale forever, even after GH#36931 (advisory) and GH#36954 (main's helper for forks). This adds a pull_request_target trigger to the self-caller and the downstream caller template. The shared eligibility matrix (identical in all three files, GH#28316 parity) now admits pull_request only for same-repository PRs and pull_request_target only for fork PRs, so there is exactly one evaluator per push. Safety: for forks the reusable workflow checks out only marcusquinn/aidevops scripts at main (aidevops_ref resolves to main for forks), never PR code. Attacker-controlled fields reach shell only via env:. The only ${{ }} in a run: block is the head SHA.



## Files Changed

.agents/reference/review-bot-gate.md, .agents/scripts/tests/test-reusable-workflow-caller.sh, .agents/templates/workflows/review-bot-gate-caller.yml, .github/workflows/review-bot-gate-reusable.yml, .github/workflows/review-bot-gate.yml

## Decisions

Chose pull_request_target over a workflow_run status relay. A relay would have to trust the fork run's conclusion, and a fork can change the workflow file used by its own pull_request run. pull_request_target evaluates base-branch YAML and main's helper only.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** High
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Runtime reproduction of the bug: #36845 head 918edf4761, Review Bot Gate run 42284687451 (pull_request, fork) logged aidevops_ref: main and Helper result: PASS_RATE_LIMITED, then gh: Resource not accessible by integration (HTTP 403) on the status post. No review-bot-gate status exists on that head. pull_request_target always runs the base-branch workflow, so the new trigger can only run for real after merge. Post-merge check: the next push to #36845 must produce a pull_request_target gate run that posts review-bot-gate=success. Static: actionlint clean on both workflows; shellcheck clean; markdownlint 0. test-reusable-workflow-caller.sh 26/26 with pyyaml, including the eligibility matrix plus new fork fixtures (same-repo pull_request yes, fork pull_request no, fork pull_request_target yes, same-repo pull_request_target no, bot issue_comment on fork yes). test-linked-issue-guidance.sh and test-review-bot-gate-issue-sync-trust.sh pass. test-check-workflows-classifier.sh 1/20, which also fails on main.

Resolves #36961

title: GH#36921: fix(lifecycle): release writer lock during archive I/O
body:
## Summary

For #36921 — partial delivery, not resolution of every contention source.

Release the global SQLite writer only during non-destructive legacy archive capture and verification. Retain the per-operation lock, reacquire `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, and revalidate exact registered writers before journaling progress or proceeding to removal. Native move and deletion remain under the writer lock. The existing two-second busy timeout is unchanged.

## Files Changed

- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/worker_lifecycle/legacy_cleanup.py`: bounded archive-I/O transaction scopes and mandatory registry revalidation
- `.agents/worker-lifecycle/tests/test_legacy_cleanup.py`: independent SQLite admission connections, racing enrollment, reacquisition failure/retry, and native move/removal exclusion

## Decisions

Keep #36921 open: reconstructible cleanup still holds the writer across network queries and restore-probe work. This PR demonstrates and repairs the archive-I/O case only. The source of the historical live lock is not independently proven. No live registry mutation, non-fixture worktree deletion, release, or activation is included.

Every new unlock point follows read-only validation or an already committed checkpoint; it does not publish a successful retirement. Keep the operation lock and physical directory handles across the unlocked scope. Reacquisition failure aborts cleanup, including when an archive artifact exists without a journal receipt. Registered-writer drift stops the operation before native move/removal; source fingerprint and physical identity guards remain intact.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** High
- **Verification:** runtime-verified
- Before the repair, a real second SQLite connection attempting unrelated admission during archive capture fails with `OperationalError`, category `contention`, after the existing two-second timeout.
- `umask 077` followed by `PYTHONPATH=.agents/worker-lifecycle python3 -m unittest tests.test_legacy_cleanup tests.test_admission tests.test_failure_category`: all 58 tests pass.
- New checks cover unrelated admission during capture and both verification stages; replay returns false rather than authorizing another execution; same-source enrollment during capture/final verification retains the source; writer reacquisition timeout leaves no archive/plan/retired journal success and retries safely; native move and removal still exclude a second SQLite writer.
- Existing archive failure, source drift, incomplete-retirement retry, and restore checks pass in the same suite.
- CI-pinned Ruff 0.11.13 passes for `.agents/worker-lifecycle`; changed-file local gates and push-time typecheck pass.
